  • Performance notes and the C++ API reference

Performance notes and the C++ API reference

Performance notes

rayrai defaults to one simulation/render thread. Applications that explicitly opt into ThreadingMode::MultiThread use one renderer and current OpenGL context per worker, as described in rayrai Visualizer. The renderer keeps the main performance controls explicit:

  • Disable shadows for high-throughput camera observations when shadows are not part of the desired output. Use RenderOverrides::doShadows = false or disable the light’s shadow map globally.

  • Prefer addInstancedVisuals for repeated primitives or meshes. A single instanced visual renders many copies with one instance buffer instead of many separate visual objects.

  • Opaque RaiSim single-body primitives (spheres, boxes, cylinders, capsules) are batched into instanced draws in shadow-map passes and in simple-shading color passes. With PBR primitives (Balanced and above) the color pass batches them only in renders without shadows.

  • TCP viewer scenes synthesize repeated articulated mesh visuals into internal InstancedVisuals batches when mesh path, scale, color policy, and color match. RemoteScene::tcpMeshBatchCount() and tcpMeshBatchMeshColorCount() expose diagnostics for this path.

  • Use InstancedVisuals::setMaxRenderedInstances and PointCloud::setMaxRenderedPoints as simple LOD caps for debug overlays, particles, scans, or dense markers that do not need full density in every frame.

  • Keep non-visible debug geometry outside the camera frustum when possible. rayrai performs coarse frustum culling for RaiSim objects, custom visuals, instanced visuals, and point clouds, so off-camera content is skipped before draw submission. Mesh-local bounds are used when available, so offset meshes, articulated links, deformables, and heightmaps cull and frame from their rendered bounds rather than only from the object origin.

  • Scenes with many local lights can give point, spot and area lights a finite range with additionalLightContributionThreshold (see Render quality, tone mapping, color grading).

  • If the world topology is stable, repeated updateObjectLists() calls are cheap: rayrai refreshes appearances without rebuilding the object cache unless objects were added or removed.

  • RGB/depth CPU readback supports an optional PBO-backed asynchronous path. The synchronous path remains the deterministic default for simple RL loops.

  • Dynamic point clouds and instanced visuals support partial buffer updates for streaming changes.

  • Deformable TCP streaming sends topology/indices only during initialization or topology changes; normal frames send vertex positions only.

GPU paths and OpenGL requirements

Several instanced-rendering paths run on the GPU when the context supports them and fall back automatically otherwise:

  • Instanced visuals with 4096 or more rendered instances are culled with a compute shader (OpenGL 4.3). Without it, culling runs on the CPU.

  • Instanced meshes made of several submeshes can be submitted with multi-draw-indirect (OpenGL 4.3 or GL_ARB_multi_draw_indirect); otherwise each submesh is drawn separately.

  • Foliage visuals with 4096 or more instances are occlusion-culled against opaque geometry already drawn in the frame, using a hierarchical depth pyramid or occlusion queries. The compute-shader pyramid needs OpenGL 4.3.

  • With OpenGL 4.3 and MSAA, foliage is also culled against the depth rendered so far in the same frame (see Dense foliage).

Most of these fallbacks print a one-time WARN line to stderr; the matching RAYRAI_SUPPRESS_*_FALLBACK_WARNINGS variable silences it (see Environment variables).

macOS provides OpenGL 4.1 (no compute shaders or multi-draw-indirect), so it uses the fallback of every path above; see Platform support. The renderer also selects a full, compact or limited shader tier from the number of fragment texture units when it is constructed; the lower tiers render fewer material and post-process features (see GPU capability tiers).

Dense foliage

Instanced visuals with alpha-masked foliage materials use a dedicated path with no extra API calls:

  • Compatible foliage draws in the color and shadow passes are merged into batched runs. Other objects between them split a run instead of disabling batching.

  • Visibility, and for larger plants the LOD level, are chosen per instance and per submesh from the automatic mesh LOD chain. A level is used when its projected simplification error is at most 2.25 pixels, or 2.5 shadow-map texels in shadow passes. RAYRAI_FOLIAGE_LOD_PIXEL_ERROR and RAYRAI_FOLIAGE_SHADOW_LOD_PIXEL_ERROR override these budgets for the whole process (values in (0, 8]).

  • With OpenGL 4.3 and MSAA, passes that contain a foliage visual with 2048 or more instances cull foliage against the depth already rendered in the same frame, tested in 8-pixel tiles that cover every sample.

  • Foliage casts shadows by default. Call setCastsShadows(false) on an InstancedVisuals to exclude it; wind and grass-patch configuration keep that choice. When the main viewer refreshes cascaded shadows every frame, foliage that cannot shadow anything inside a cascade’s part of the view is skipped for that cascade.

  • With asynchronous mesh loading (Capture, diagnostics, and headless rendering), base geometry and instanced LOD chains are prepared on worker threads. Each pollAsyncMeshLoads(n) call advances at most n import/upload stages (0 does nothing) and uploads at most one prepared submesh per pending instanced visual; pendingAsyncMeshLoadCount() includes these jobs. Prepared LOD chains are cached on disk (see On-disk caches).

  • rayrai/Bc7TextureStorage.hpp provides an opt-in load-time helper, raisin::compressRgbTextureBc7(texture), that re-stores an RGB8/SRGB8 texture and all of its mip levels as BC7. It needs OpenGL 4.2 or GL_ARB_texture_compression_bptc (check supportsBc7TextureStorage()) and is lossy. Alpha, float, immutable and already compressed textures are left unchanged.

Frame submission and measurement

The renderer applies these submission optimizations automatically; none of them changes the rendered image:

  • After shadow maps or the planar reflection were rendered in a frame, one glFlush submits them so the GPU works on them while the CPU encodes the scene pass. This lowers frame time at the cost of some process CPU time. The RAYRAI_DEBUG_DISABLE_PASS_FLUSH=1 debug switch skips this flush.

  • The environment background is drawn inside the scene pass. After an opaque depth prepass it is depth-tested, so only pixels that no surface covers are shaded. environmentBackgroundDiagnostics() reports how the last scene pass drew it.

  • The transparent pass skips the proximity-fade depth copy and the screen-space refraction capture when no drawn material samples them.

  • An external Camera keeps its multisampled render target between frames; the next render of that camera without MSAA releases it. Camera::setSceneMsaaSamples(samples, keepAllocation) exposes the same behavior.

While RenderQualitySettings::geometryRefraction is on, the frame caches that let unchanged external-camera renders reuse earlier results are bypassed, so every render is drawn in full.

captureViewerPassTimings(width, height) renders the built-in viewer camera once with blocking GPU timer queries (the renderer’s context must be current) and returns the shadow, scene_color_and_resolve and postprocess passes. captureRenderPassTimings does the same for an external camera. When foliage instanced visuals are present, both render a second frame and append shadow_foliage* and scene_foliage* entries that are nested inside the coarse passes. shadowCacheDiagnostics(), foliageRenderDiagnostics() and conservativeOcclusionCullingDiagnostics() report shadow-map reuse and culling without extra GPU work.

Shared mesh buffers across contexts

OpenGL contexts in one share group reuse the immutable vertex/index buffers of the built-in primitives and of file-backed meshes whose materials use no textures and no nextPass chain. To create such contexts, make the root SDL OpenGL context current before calling RayraiWindow::createOffscreenGlContext for each child. Each call makes the new context current, so rebind the root when creating the next child. Creating a context on a thread with no current context creates an independent share group and cannot provide this reuse.

Textures are not shared. rayrai sets filtering and anisotropy on each texture object per material and per quality preset, so every context decodes and uploads its own copy of each image file, and textured meshes are uploaded per context as well.

Keep each renderer’s context current for rendering and resource destruction. Do not use one context concurrently on multiple threads. VAOs, framebuffers, and camera targets remain specific to each context. A context created on the main thread stays current there; release it with RayraiWindow::detachOffscreenGlContext(window) before a worker adopts it with makeOffscreenContextCurrent. The cache retains weak references, so reuse requires an existing owner to keep the mesh alive.

The public diagnostics can be read without changing rendering behavior:

const auto stats = raisin::RayraiGlobalAsset::sharedGpuAssetStats();
const auto uploadedBytes = stats.gpuBufferBytesUploaded;
const auto reusedBytes = stats.gpuBufferBytesReused;
const auto templates = stats.cachedSnapshots;

The byte counts are cumulative mesh-buffer counters, not total or live GPU memory. Textures, VAOs, and render targets are excluded. cachedSnapshots is the number of published mesh templates currently held, one per distinct asset and share group. Use resetSharedGpuAssetStats() before a controlled measurement. The cache is enabled by default; setSharedGpuAssetCacheEnabled(false) makes every later mesh lookup upload its own buffers.

Shader binary cache and multi-threaded prewarming

rayrai’s PBR shaders compile in 10-30 seconds on first run depending on the GL driver. Two features (available since v2.3.0) remove that wait in production RL pipelines:

  1. Persistent shader binary cache. Compiled GL programs are written to a per-driver cache directory and reloaded on subsequent runs.

  2. Static prewarm helper for multi-threaded RL setups where many worker threads will each construct their own RayraiWindow — one thread can pre-compile every shader, then every worker thread reads from the cache.

Both are wired through the RayraiWindow constructor:

raisin::RayraiWindow viewer(
  world,
  /*width=*/1280, /*height=*/720,
  raisin::RayraiWindow::ThreadingMode::SingleThread,
  /*shaderCompileThreadCount=*/1,            // 1 = matches rayrai's default
  /*shaderBinaryCacheEnabled=*/true,         // on by default
  /*shaderBinaryCacheDirectory=*/"",          // empty → default location
  /*logShaderBinaryCache=*/false);

  • shaderCompileThreadCount is passed to glMaxShaderCompilerThreadsARB on drivers that expose GL_ARB_parallel_shader_compile and is ignored elsewhere. Raise it only when the host application is itself multi-threaded.

  • shaderBinaryCacheEnabled = true (the default) writes program binaries under the cache directory keyed by GL vendor / renderer / version + GLSL source, when the driver reports at least one program binary format. On the next run, identical configurations are loaded directly, skipping the GLSL compile entirely. Several processes can share one cache directory.

  • shaderBinaryCacheDirectory = "" uses the first writable directory in this order, then falls back to <temp>/raisim/rayrai:

    • Linux: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/raisim/rayrai, ~/.cache/raisim/rayrai, ~/.raisim/rayrai

    • macOS: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/raisim/rayrai, ~/Library/Caches/raisim/rayrai, ~/.cache/raisim/rayrai, ~/.raisim/rayrai

    • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\RaiSim\rayrai, %HOME%\.raisim\rayrai (when HOME is set), %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\RaiSim\rayrai, %USERPROFILE%\.raisim\rayrai

  • logShaderBinaryCache = true prints every hit/miss/store to stderr — useful for verifying the cache is actually being consulted.

The compile thread count and the cache settings are process-wide: each RayraiWindow constructor applies its arguments to the whole process, so pass the same values to every renderer, including a prewarmer.

Cache statistics (per process, across all Shader::compile calls):

auto s = raisin::Shader::binaryCacheStats();
std::printf("hits=%llu misses=%llu stores=%llu coordinated_waits=%llu\n",
            static_cast<unsigned long long>(s.hits),
            static_cast<unsigned long long>(s.misses),
            static_cast<unsigned long long>(s.stores),
            static_cast<unsigned long long>(s.coordinatedWaits));
raisin::Shader::resetBinaryCacheStats();  // scope a measurement window

Pre-warming for parallel RL can be done with the rayrai_shader_prewarm utility when it is available in the rayrai package. The utility creates an offscreen context and compiles every built-in shader into the persistent binary cache:

rayrai_shader_prewarm --cache-dir /tmp/rayrai-cache --compile-threads 4 --multi-thread
rayrai_shader_prewarm --log-cache

For an embedded application, create an offscreen context on the main thread, release it, and call prewarmShadersForCurrentContext once from a background thread that adopts it. SDL windows must be created and destroyed on the main thread, and every renderer in the process, including the prewarmer, must use the same ThreadingMode. Worker threads that later construct their own RayraiWindow will find the heavy shaders already cached (or briefly block on a per-shader compile mutex if the warm-up is still in flight):

// Main thread: create the prewarm context, then release it.
SDL_Window* w = nullptr;
SDL_GLContext gl = nullptr;
raisin::RayraiWindow::createOffscreenGlContext(w, gl, "rayrai_prewarm");
raisin::RayraiWindow::detachOffscreenGlContext(w);

std::thread prewarm([w, gl] {
  raisin::RayraiWindow::makeOffscreenContextCurrent(w, gl);
  raisin::RayraiWindow::prewarmShadersForCurrentContext(
    raisin::RayraiWindow::ThreadingMode::MultiThread);
  raisin::RayraiWindow::detachOffscreenGlContext(w);
});

// ... start the rendering workers ...

prewarm.join();  // main thread
SDL_GL_DeleteContext(gl);
SDL_DestroyWindow(w);

Pass the workers’ cache directory as the second argument of prewarmShadersForCurrentContext when they do not use the default location. With the binary cache enabled, each registered program is compiled from GLSL once per process, however many worker threads construct renderers.

When you only want to warm a specific subset:

// Names of every program registered with the running RayraiWindow.
auto names = viewer.linkedShaderNames();

// Compile the heaviest authored-content shader explicitly.
long long ms = viewer.compileShaderByName("pbrMeshHigh");
std::printf("pbrMeshHigh warmup: %lld ms\n", ms);

// Iterate every program, one per call. `done` flips true when all are
// linked; useful for spreading shader work across multiple frames.
bool done = false;
while (!done) {
  viewer.warmupNextShader(done);
}

For diagnostics on the cost of the lazy-compile pipeline (how long each program took on first use, how many are linked so far), call shaderWarmupDiagnostics().

On-disk caches

Besides the shader binary cache, rayrai keeps these caches. All of them are regenerated when missing, so the files can be deleted at any time. The mesh caches are also checked against their source and rebuilt when stale.

Contents

Default location

Override

Imported-mesh metadata and generated LOD chains

<temp>/rayrai_mesh_preprocess_cache

RAYRAI_MESH_PREPROCESS_CACHE_DIR

LOD chains prepared by asynchronous loading of instanced meshes

rayrai_cache_<file>.lods next to the source asset, else <temp>/rayrai_async_lod_cache

RAYRAI_ASYNC_LOD_CACHE_DIR

Procedural cloud noise textures

$HOME/.raisim/rayrai, then %USERPROFILE%\.raisim\rayrai (Windows), then <temp>/raisim/rayrai

RAYRAI_CLOUD_TEXTURE_CACHE_DIR

<temp> is the system temporary directory. The asynchronous LOD sidecars store full vertex data and can be large for dense assets.

Environment variables

rayrai reads these variables from the process environment; set them before the renderer starts. Boolean switches are on when set to a non-empty value that does not start with 0, unless noted otherwise.

  • RAYRAI_MESH_PREPROCESS_CACHE_DIR, RAYRAI_ASYNC_LOD_CACHE_DIR, RAYRAI_CLOUD_TEXTURE_CACHE_DIR: cache directories (see On-disk caches).

  • RAYRAI_FOLIAGE_LOD_PIXEL_ERROR and RAYRAI_FOLIAGE_SHADOW_LOD_PIXEL_ERROR: foliage LOD error budgets (defaults 2.25 pixels and 2.5 texels; read once per process). The shadow budget follows the color budget when only the latter is set.

  • RAYRAI_SUPPRESS_<PATH>_FALLBACK_WARNINGS: silence the one-time warning of a GPU path fallback, for example RAYRAI_SUPPRESS_GPU_INSTANCE_CULLING_FALLBACK_WARNINGS.

  • RAYRAI_FORCE_COMPACT_PBR_SAMPLER_FALLBACK and RAYRAI_FORCE_LIMITED_PBR_SAMPLER_FALLBACK: select the compact or limited shader tier on a larger GPU, for testing.

  • RAYRAI_EAGER_SHADER_WARMUP: compile every registered shader when a renderer is constructed instead of on first use.

  • RAYRAI_PBR_DEBUG_OUTPUT: PBR debug visualization channel (0 is off). RayraiWindow::setPbrDebugOutputMode overrides it for one renderer, and captureDebugPasses overrides it for the frames it renders.

The TCP viewer reads its own RAYRAI_TCP_VIEWER_* variables (Rayrai TCP Viewer). Variables named RAYRAI_DEBUG_* and RAYRAI_LOG_* are renderer-development diagnostics (debug switches and logging) and may change between releases. Apart from these debug switches, optimizations have no switches to turn them off.

Additional tips

  • Every update and external-camera render calls RayraiWindow::updateObjectLists(), so RaiSim objects added to or removed from the world are picked up automatically. Call it yourself only when the renderer’s object lists must be current before the next render.

  • Use setShowCollisionBodies(true) for debug visualization of collision shapes.

  • If you want rayrai overlays to use your ImGui font, pass it via setExternalFont.

API

Core types

class RayraiWindow

Offscreen renderer and visual scene manager for raisim.

RayraiWindow maintains an internal Camera, shader set, and a set of visual objects that can be rendered into an offscreen texture. It can render raisim world objects, custom visuals, point clouds, and coordinate frames.



Quick start
auto world = std::make_shared<raisim::World>();
world->addSphere(0.5, 1.0);

// A GL context must be current first, e.g.:
//   SDL_Window* win; SDL_GLContext ctx;
//   raisin::RayraiWindow::createOffscreenGlContext(win, ctx);
raisin::RayraiWindow renderer(world, 1280, 720);

// Add a free-standing visual using the glm::vec4 colour overload.
renderer.addVisualSphere("marker", 0.25, glm::vec4(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));

// (Optional) IBL: one struct instead of four GL handles.
auto env = raisin::PbrEnvironment::loadFromHdrFile("studio.hdr");

// Drive the simulation and render one frame.
world->integrate();
renderer.update(1280, 720, false, 0, 0, false);
unsigned int textureId = renderer.getImageTexture();



Lifetime

The shared_ptr constructor stores the pointer, so the window shares ownership of the world and keeps it alive. The raisim::World& constructor wraps the reference in a non-owning shared_ptr; that world must outlive the window (or be replaced with swapWorld() before it is destroyed).



GL context

Construction, rendering, resource creation (textures, cubemaps, probes) and destruction issue OpenGL calls, so they must run on the thread that has this renderer’s GL context current (see createOffscreenGlContext()). The pure-CPU helpers (e.g. analyzeRgbaLuminance(), recommendExposure(), loadReflectionProbeSidecar()) do not touch GL.



Error model

Named entities are strict: addVisual*(), addInstancedVisuals(), addPointCloud() and addCoordinateFrame() abort (RSFATAL) when the name is already in use, and getVisualObject(), getInstancedVisuals(), removeVisualObject(), removeInstancedVisuals(), removePointCloud() and removeCoordinateFrame() abort when it does not exist. Use findVisualObject() / findInstancedVisuals() for a lookup that returns nullptr instead. A few newer entry points throw std::invalid_argument instead of aborting; this is noted on each of them.

The texture and cubemap loaders (loadTextureWithTiling(), loadHdrEquirectangularCubemap(), …) return 0 on failure.

Threading-mode mismatch at construction is fatal (RSFATAL).

Weather

While WeatherSettings::enabled is true, the resolved weather is applied on top of the last settings passed to setRenderQualitySettings(): main light, ambient, sky, clouds and wet/snow materials are overwritten and fog is combined with the user values (see raisin::WeatherSettings). Disabling weather restores the user settings; getUserRenderQualitySettings() returns them meanwhile. Transitions and wetness advance only in updateWeather().

using WeatherThunderCallback = std::function<void(const WeatherDiagnostics&)>

Callback invoked from updateWeather() once per new lightning event.

void setWeatherSettings(const WeatherSettings &settings)

Apply weather settings immediately.

Values are clamped to their valid ranges, any running transition is cancelled, a generated weather sky environment is released, and the render quality settings are updated (see the group description).

Parameters:

settings – New weather settings.

inline const WeatherSettings &getWeatherSettings() const
Returns:

Current (clamped) weather settings; mid-transition this is the blended state.

void setWeatherThunderCallback(WeatherThunderCallback callback)

Register the lightning/thunder callback (empty function to remove).

Called synchronously on the thread that calls updateWeather(), with the diagnostics of the frame in which a new lightning event started.

Parameters:

callback – Callback to store.

void setWeatherPreset(WeatherPreset preset)

Apply defaultWeatherSettings(preset) immediately.

Parameters:

preset – Preset to apply.

void transitionWeather(WeatherPreset preset, double transitionSeconds)

Blend from the current weather to a preset’s defaults over time.

Parameters:

  • preset – Target preset.

  • transitionSeconds – Duration; <= 0 applies the target immediately.

void transitionWeather(const WeatherSettings &target, double transitionSeconds)

Blend from the current weather to target over time.

The blend advances only in updateWeather().

Parameters:

  • target – Target settings.

  • transitionSeconds – Duration in seconds; <= 0 applies the target immediately.

void updateWeather(double dt)

Advance weather transitions, wetness accumulation/drying and lightning.

Call once per frame from the render thread before rendering.

Parameters:

dt – Elapsed time in seconds (negative values are treated as 0).

WeatherDiagnostics weatherDiagnostics() const

Resolved weather state (sun/moon, clouds, fog, precipitation, wetness, lightning). CPU only.

Returns:

Diagnostics for the current settings.

void printWeatherDiagnostics(std::ostream &out) const

Print weatherDiagnostics() in a human-readable multi-line form.

Parameters:

out – Output stream.

WeatherSkyEnvironment generateWeatherSkyEnvironment(int environmentFaceSize = 256, int irradianceFaceSize = 32, bool setVisibleBackground = true)

Generate a weather-driven sky/environment cubemap on demand.

This is intentionally explicit. Applications should call it at weather or time-of-day transition points, not every frame. When setVisibleBackground is true, the generated radiance cubemap is also installed as the visible environment background. The previous generated environment is released first; the textures are owned by the renderer and are also released by clearWeatherSkyEnvironment() and setWeatherSettings(). Requires this renderer’s GL context.

Parameters:

  • environmentFaceSize – Radiance cubemap face size, clamped to [16, 2048].

  • irradianceFaceSize – Irradiance cubemap face size, clamped to [0, 256]; 0 skips it.

  • setVisibleBackground – Install the radiance map as the visible background.

Returns:

The generated environment (also available via weatherSkyEnvironment()).

void clearWeatherSkyEnvironment()

Delete the generated weather sky textures; unsets the visible background if it was installed.

inline const WeatherSkyEnvironment &weatherSkyEnvironment() const
Returns:

Last generated weather sky environment (valid false when none).

static WeatherSettings defaultWeatherSettings(WeatherPreset preset)

Default settings for a weather preset (CPU only).

Parameters:

preset – Preset to expand.

Returns:

Settings with enabled = true, High quality, 13:00 local time.

Internal: static/dynamic layer dirty rect

NDC bounds of the previous frame’s dynamic AABB union, used to compute a conservative scissor rect for the current frame’s dynamic redraw. Not part of the supported API.

Internal: previous dynamic-layer NDC minimum x.

mutable float lastDynamicLayerNdcMinY_

Internal: previous dynamic-layer NDC minimum y.

mutable float lastDynamicLayerNdcMaxX_

Internal: previous dynamic-layer NDC maximum x.

mutable float lastDynamicLayerNdcMaxY_

Internal: previous dynamic-layer NDC maximum y.

mutable bool lastDynamicLayerDirtyRectValid_

Internal: the four bounds above are valid.

Ground and heightmap terrain textures

inline void setHeightmapSplatLayer(const std::string &albedoPath, unsigned int controlTexId, float primaryUvScale, float secondaryUvScale, const glm::vec4 &controlBounds)

Configure a secondary terrain splat layer for heightmap meshes.

The PBR mesh shader blends albedoPath over the primary heightmap albedo using a single-channel control texture. Setting controlTexId to 0 or albedoPath empty disables splat blending. Blending only happens when a primary albedo (setHeightmapPatternResourcePath()) is set as well.

Parameters:

  • albedoPath – Secondary albedo image (sRGB); reloaded only when the path changes.

  • controlTexId – Single-channel control texture (e.g. from updateSingleChannelTexture()); its red channel is the secondary weight (0 = primary only, 1 = secondary only). Not owned. All coordinates below are world XY of the terrain as if it were unrotated (its translation applied, its orientation ignored), like raisim::HeightMap::getHeight(); for a rotated heightmap the layer therefore turns with the terrain.

  • primaryUvScale – Primary albedo tiling: UV = world XY * scale (default 0.25).

  • secondaryUvScale – Secondary albedo tiling: UV = world XY * scale (default 0.25).

  • controlBounds – World XY rectangle covered by the control texture as (minX, minY, sizeX, sizeY) in metres; outside it the edge value is used.

Custom visuals

Render-only shapes that are not part of raisim::World. Names share one namespace (addVisual*(), importVisualScene(), addCameraFrustum()) and must be unique (RSFATAL otherwise). Sizes are in metres, colors are RGBA in [0, 1]. A new visual sits at the world origin with identity orientation; move it through the returned Visuals. The renderer keeps its own reference until removeVisualObject(), clearVisualizationObjects() or swapWorld().

Public Types

enum class ThreadingMode

Threading contract for the renderer.

SingleThread (the default) promises the application creates exactly one RayraiWindow per process and never spawns additional threads that touch rayrai state. Render state is owned by the window or the calling thread.

MultiThread is for RL / batch-render setups that spawn one RayraiWindow per worker thread, each with its own offscreen GL context. State that would otherwise need synchronization is owned by the object it describes — a resolved uniform location by its Shader, GL context state by the renderer driving that context — rather than kept per-thread, so handing a context between threads does not strand it. Shared resources (immutable mesh templates and shader compilation) are coordinated. File textures and mutable material state are local to each worker/context.

This is instance confinement, not concurrent access to one window. Construct, render, read back, edit, and destroy a renderer on its owning worker with its GL context current. Do not integrate or mutate its World on another thread while rendering. Prefer an independent World per worker. Keep application supplied mutable materials, cameras, visuals and GPU objects worker-local. Create/destroy SDL windows on the main thread and hand their contexts to workers with makeOffscreenContextCurrent after detaching them on the main thread. All renderers in the process, including prewarmers, must use this mode.

What workers share and what they duplicate: immutable mesh geometry is shared between contexts in one GL share group, so a model imported by one worker costs no second vertex/index upload. Textures are not: rayrai retunes filtering and anisotropy on the texture object itself, per material and per render-quality preset, so a shared texture would let one worker’s settings rewrite another’s. Each worker therefore decodes and uploads its own copy of every image, and a textured model’s geometry is not shared either. Lifting that needs filtering to move off the texture object onto GL sampler objects bound per texture unit.

Mixing the two — for example, constructing several SingleThread windows on different threads — is unsupported.

Values:

enumerator SingleThread

One renderer per process, driven from one thread (default).

enumerator MultiThread

One renderer per worker thread, each with its own GL context.

Public Functions

RayraiWindow(std::shared_ptr<raisim::World> world, int width = 300, int height = 300, ThreadingMode threadingMode = ThreadingMode::SingleThread, unsigned int shaderCompileThreadCount = 1u, bool shaderBinaryCacheEnabled = true, std::string shaderBinaryCacheDirectory = std::string{}, bool logShaderBinaryCache = false)

Construct an offscreen renderer tied to a raisim world.

Requires a current OpenGL context on the calling thread (see createOffscreenGlContext()); built-in shaders are registered here and the viewer render targets are allocated lazily on first render.

Parameters:

  • world – Shared world pointer used for pulling object state. The window keeps this shared_ptr, i.e. it shares ownership.

  • width – Initial render target width in pixels.

  • height – Initial render target height in pixels.

  • threadingMode – Concurrency contract — see ThreadingMode. Must match every other RayraiWindow in the process (RSFATAL otherwise).

  • shaderCompileThreadCount – Driver-side shader compile threads (passed to glMaxShaderCompilerThreadsARB); 0 is treated as 1. Defaults to 1 to match rayrai’s overall single-threaded default; raise this only when the host application explicitly opts into multi-threading. This is a process-wide setting shared by all renderers.

  • shaderBinaryCacheEnabled – When true, compiled shader programs are persisted under shaderBinaryCacheDirectory and reused on next run, skipping driver compile entirely for unchanged GLSL/driver. Process-wide, like the two parameters below.

  • shaderBinaryCacheDirectory – Explicit cache directory. Empty selects the first writable per-user cache directory: LOCALAPPDATA%/RaiSim/rayrai on Windows, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/raisim/rayrai, ~/Library/Caches/raisim/rayrai (macOS) or ~/.cache/raisim/rayrai, then ~/.raisim/rayrai, then the system temp directory.

  • logShaderBinaryCache – When true, cache hits/misses/stores are logged to stderr — useful when verifying that the cache is actually being consulted.

RayraiWindow(raisim::World &world, int width = 300, int height = 300, ThreadingMode threadingMode = ThreadingMode::SingleThread, unsigned int shaderCompileThreadCount = 1u, bool shaderBinaryCacheEnabled = true, std::string shaderBinaryCacheDirectory = std::string{}, bool logShaderBinaryCache = false)

Construct an offscreen renderer tied to a raisim world (non-owning).

Same as the shared_ptr overload, but world is wrapped with a no-op deleter: the caller keeps ownership and the world must outlive this window (or be replaced with swapWorld() first).

Parameters:

  • world – World reference used for pulling object state.

  • width – Initial render target width in pixels.

  • height – Initial render target height in pixels.

  • threadingMode – Concurrency contract — see ThreadingMode.

  • shaderCompileThreadCount – Process-wide driver shader compile threads.

  • shaderBinaryCacheEnabled – Enable the process-wide shader binary cache.

  • shaderBinaryCacheDirectory – Explicit cache directory; empty selects the default per-user cache directory.

  • logShaderBinaryCache – Log cache hits/misses/stores to stderr.

void swapWorld(std::shared_ptr<raisim::World> world)

Reset this renderer to host a different raisim::World, reusing compiled shaders, textures, and render targets.

Pointers into the previous world become invalid the moment the caller destroys it, so this method drops every renderer-side handle that referenced those objects (per-object draw wrappers, render/shadow candidate caches, picking ids, the target visual and camera targets) and every visual added via addVisualXxx / addInstancedVisuals / addPointCloud / addCoordinateFrame, plus tendon visuals. Additional lights, fog volumes, projected decals, irradiance volumes, and registered reflection probes are cleared so the caller’s scene-application step can repopulate them (probe textures are not deleted). Camera and render-quality settings are preserved.

The dropped visuals are kept alive (unreferenced by the renderer) until the end of the next update(), renderWithExternalCamera(), or depth-only render, so a scene applied again in between reuses their meshes, mesh LODs and foliage partitions instead of reading and processing every model again. Models whose files changed since they were read are read again (RayraiGlobalAsset::forgetChangedModelFiles()).

Parameters:

world – New world; stored (shared ownership) like the constructor’s.

Enable or disable async mesh file import for future mesh visuals/world assets.

Async loading parses files and prepares base geometry and instanced LODs on workers. Pending instances are skipped; textures and incremental GPU uploads use the render thread. Disable it when a caller needs mesh assets to be available immediately after addVisualMesh()/importVisualScene(). Enabled by default; USD files are always imported synchronously.

inline std::shared_ptr<const void> modelHandle(const std::string &meshFile) const

A strong reference to a model file this renderer has read.

The model caches reference models weakly, and instanced foliage keeps only the meshes it derives from its model, so a model can be released while the scene still uses it. An application that rebuilds its scene (swapWorld(), then the same visuals again) can hold these handles across the rebuild, so the models are reused instead of read and prepared again.

Returns:

The model, or nullptr when it was not read (it is not read here).

inline void setKeyboardShortcutsEnabled(bool enabled)

Whether this renderer reacts to global keyboard shortcuts.

The renderer’s built-in shortcuts read SDL’s keyboard state, which is one array for the whole process and carries no notion of which window has focus. A process running several renderers would otherwise see a key press act on all of them at once, so a multi-window application should leave this on only for the focused renderer. Defaults to true, which is the behaviour of a single-renderer application. Currently the only shortcut is B, which toggles the picking-buffer debug view. Camera movement keys are controlled separately by setKeyboardInputEnabled().

Parameters:

enabled – False to ignore shortcut keys in this renderer.

inline bool keyboardShortcutsEnabled() const
Returns:

True when this renderer reacts to global keyboard shortcuts (default true).

inline int pbrDebugOutputMode() const

PBR debug output mode in force for this renderer.

The environment variable RAYRAI_PBR_DEBUG_OUTPUT sets it process-wide; captureDebugPasses overrides it for the frames it renders. The override belongs to this renderer: rewriting the process environment raced every other worker’s getenv on the render path, and a thread-local override would follow whichever thread happened to drive the renderer.

Returns:

Active mode; 0 is normal shading.

void update(int w, int h, bool isHovering, int cX, int cY, bool shouldClick)

Render one frame into the internal camera’s offscreen texture.

The interactive viewer path: resizes the target to w x h, finalizes at most one pending async mesh import, syncs raisim objects, applies mouse and keyboard camera input, then renders shadows, the scene and post-processing. Read the result with getImageTexture(). Requires this renderer’s GL context.

Parameters:

  • w – Target width in pixels.

  • h – Target height in pixels.

  • isHovering – Whether the mouse is over the render area; mouse input is ignored otherwise.

  • cX – Cursor x position inside the render area, in pixels.

  • cY – Cursor y position inside the render area, in pixels.

  • shouldClick – Whether mouse click selection should be processed.

Allow or block this renderer’s WASD/Space camera movement.

The camera reads the process-wide SDL keyboard state, which is shared by every renderer in the process. A host that draws more than one view at a time (the TCP viewer’s split panes) must therefore leave this on for just one of them, or a single key press walks every camera at once. Mouse input needs no such switch: it is already scoped by the hover flag passed to update().

void renderWithExternalCamera(raisim::RGBCamera &sensorCam, Camera &externalCam, const RenderOverrides &ov)

Render using a raisim RGB camera and an external render camera.

Only the sensor’s world pose is copied into externalCam (see syncRaisimCameraPose(): sensor +X is the view direction, +Z is up); projection and resolution come from externalCam itself. Custom visuals, point clouds and coordinate frames are never drawn, MSAA/temporal AA/viewer upscaling are disabled, and weather effects follow WeatherSettings::affectSensors, regardless of ov.

Parameters:

  • sensorCam – Raisim RGB camera providing the pose; its pose is updated.

  • externalCam – Render camera to use for rendering; receives the output.

  • ov – Shader/toggle overrides (see RenderOverrides).

Render using a raisim depth camera’s pose and an external render camera.

Same as the RGB overload (pose only, sensor-safe overrides). This renders the color image; use renderDepthPlaneDistance() for linear depth.

  • externalCam – Render camera to use for rendering; receives the output.

  • ov – Shader/toggle overrides (see RenderOverrides).

void renderWithExternalCamera(Camera &externalCam, const RenderOverrides &ov)

Render using an external render camera.

Renders into externalCam's own render targets (allocated on first use at its configured size); read the result from the camera, e.g. its final texture. Syncs raisim objects and finalizes at most one pending async mesh import first. When nothing that affects the image has changed since the last call with the same camera, the previous frame may be reused; call invalidateExternalFrameCache() after changes the renderer cannot see. Requires this renderer’s GL context.

Parameters:

  • externalCam – Render camera to use for rendering; receives the output.

  • ov – Shader/toggle overrides (see RenderOverrides). Throws std::invalid_argument when a custom post shader is combined with reprojected temporal AA.

std::vector<DebugPassCapture> captureDebugPasses(Camera &externalCam, const RenderOverrides &ov)

Capture the standard RayRai PBR/postprocess debug pass set for any scene.

The capture uses the caller-provided camera and render overrides, temporarily switches to Ultra quality, disables temporal history/upscaling for deterministic per-pass readback, and afterwards re-applies the previous quality settings through setRenderQualitySettings() and resets the renderer-local PBR debug mode to -1 (process default). Because it goes through setRenderQualitySettings(), application-added additional lights are cleared and the preset reads Custom afterwards (see setRenderQualitySettings()). Returned pixels are top-left ordered RGBA8 buffers so callers can write PNGs or analyze them without a RayRai image writer dependency.

Parameters:

  • externalCam – Camera to render with; its size defines the capture size.

  • ov – Render overrides (temporal AA and upscaling are forced off).

Returns:

25 passes (final, material channels, lighting terms, shadows, fog, AO, …).

Parameters:

camera – Camera whose frustum is split.

Returns:

Cascade plan (see DirectionalShadowCascadePlan).

The renderer uses this plan for its 2D additional-light shadow atlas (point lights keep standalone cubemaps unless the point-shadow policy says otherwise). Calling it is CPU-only; the result depends on the shadow lights selected by the last rendered frame.

Capture a static local probe and generate irradiance, prefiltered specular, and BRDF maps.

This is an explicit bounded setup operation for High/Ultra. It does not update automatically after scene changes and does not affect Fast unless the caller uses the returned probe. Uses default capture settings and reflectionProbeFilterSettingsForCurrentQuality(), so with probe filtering disabled only the raw environment map is produced. All returned textures are owned by the caller. Pass the probe to addReflectionProbe() to make it selectable.

size_t addReflectionProbe(const ReflectionProbe &probe)

Register a captured probe for selectReflectionProbeBlend() / applyNearestReflectionProbe().

The probe is copied with radius/strength clamped to >= 0 and box projection disabled for degenerate boxes. Registered probes are not bound to visuals automatically, and the registry does not take ownership of the textures.

Parameters:

probe – Probe to register; ignored when it has no environment, irradiance or prefiltered map.

Returns:

Number of registered probes afterwards.

void clearReflectionProbes()

Unregister every probe added with addReflectionProbe(); their textures stay with the caller.

bool selectReflectionProbeBlend(const glm::vec3 &position, ReflectionProbeBlend &blend) const

Pick up to two registered probes influencing a position.

Weight per probe is strength * (1 - d / radius) inside a positive radius (0 outside), or strength / (1 + d) for radius 0, where d is the distance to the probe position, or to its box when box projection is valid. Probes at or below RenderQualitySettings::minReflectionProbeWeight are skipped; the second probe is used only when maxReflectionProbesPerSelection is 2.

Parameters:

  • position – World-space query position.

  • blend – [out] Selected probes and normalized weights.

Returns:

True when at least one probe influences the position.

ReflectionProbePlacementSuggestion suggestReflectionProbePlacementFromSceneBounds() const

Suggest a static local reflection-probe placement from current scene bounds.

This is CPU-only and non-mutating. It does not capture or register a probe; callers can use the returned position/radius/box bounds with captureFilteredReflectionProbe() or a sidecar file after explicit approval. Halfspaces and heightmaps are ignored so infinite/default grounds do not dominate imported-room probe placement. Bounds are the union of approximate bounding spheres of raisim objects, custom visuals and instanced visuals.

Returns:

Suggestion; valid is false when there is nothing to bound.

Step the viewer camera through axis-aligned orthographic views.

Switches the internal camera to orthographic projection and, on each call, moves it to the next of six views placed 2 m from the camera target on the +X, +Y, -X, -Y, +Z and -Z sides, looking at the target. It does not switch back to perspective; use getCamera().setProjectionMode() for that.

void measureSpinningLidarSingleDrawGPU(raisim::SpinningLidar &lidar, const glm::dvec3 &sensorPosW, const glm::dmat3 &sensorRotW, const raisim::Object *objectToExclude = nullptr)

Measure a spinning LiDAR on the GPU.

Advances the head with SpinningLidar::advanceSweep() (the sweep state is shared with SpinningLidar::update(), so the two can alternate) and casts the swept yaw columns against the world’s collision bodies (World::getRayCastBodies()), stores the hits in the sensor frame with lidar.setScan() and stamps the world time. The scan reproduces SpinningLidar::update(): the same columns and point order, exact intersections with primitives, heightmaps and meshes, rays starting at rangeMin, and the sensor’s own body ignored. Ranges agree to float precision (about 1e-5 of the range); a ray grazing a silhouette within that tolerance may differ. Requires this renderer’s GL context.

Parameters:

  • lidar – Raisim spinning lidar to update.

  • sensorPosW – LiDAR position in world coordinates.

  • sensorRotW – LiDAR orientation in world coordinates.

  • objectToExclude – Optional object whose bodies are all ignored (e.g. the carrier).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if a GL resource cannot be created or the scene exceeds a GPU limit.

Changing it resets temporal AA history.

Parameters:

enabled – True to enable linear HDR rendering (default false).

inline Light &getLight()

Access the main scene light (the single main shadow caster).

Direct edits take effect on the next frame, but setRenderQualitySettings(), setRenderQualityPreset(), promoteDominantAdditionalLightToMainShadowCaster() and enabled weather overwrite parts of it. Call requestShadowUpdate() after moving it when shadows are not refreshed every frame.

Returns:

Reference to the main light, owned by the renderer.

void addAdditionalLight(const AdditionalLight &light)

Add a light besides the main light.

The light is sanitized and copied. Additional lights with AdditionalLight::castsShadows set can receive shadow maps when shadows are enabled and RenderQualitySettings::shadowedLightBudget is greater than 1 (up to kMaxAdditionalShadowLights per frame); otherwise they only shade. Note that setRenderQualitySettings() / setRenderQualityPreset() clear all additional lights, so add lights after choosing the quality settings.

Parameters:

light – Additional light. Ignored once kMaxAdditionalLights lights exist.

Replace an existing additional light without forcing unrelated shadow maps dirty.

Parameters:

  • light – New light (sanitized and copied).

Returns:

True if the light existed and was replaced.

void clearAdditionalLights()

Remove all additional lights (including their shadow maps).

The main light is unaffected.

Return the current number of additional lights.

Returns:

Number of additional lights (excluding the main light).

bool promoteDominantAdditionalLightToMainShadowCaster(bool preferSpotLights = true, bool removePromotedAdditionalLight = true)

Promote the dominant imported/local light to the single shadow-casting main light.

This is intended for authored glTF scenes that have a clear lamp/spot light. It keeps low-quality rendering fast because no additional shadow maps are created. Candidates must have AdditionalLight::castsShadows set and non-zero power; point lights are never promoted (they use cubemap shadows through the additional-light budget). The main light takes over the candidate’s type, pose, color and attenuation, and its shadows are enabled.

Parameters:

  • preferSpotLights – Prefer spot lights over other light types when possible.

  • removePromotedAdditionalLight – Remove the promoted light from the additional-light list to avoid double-counting its direct contribution.

Returns:

True if a suitable light was promoted.

size_t importSceneLights(const std::string &sceneFile, float intensityScale = 1.0f)

Import authored scene lights from a mesh/scene file through Assimp.

Imported lights are appended as additional lights (see addAdditionalLight()). This is explicit so low-quality rendering does not pay for scene lights unless an application imports them. When any light was added and RenderQualitySettings::autoSelectImportedShadowLight is set with a non-zero shadowedLightBudget, the dominant one is promoted to the main shadow caster. Import errors are printed to stderr, not thrown.

Parameters:

  • sceneFile – Scene/mesh file to read lights from.

  • intensityScale – Multiplier applied to imported light intensities.

Returns:

Number of lights appended, capped by kMaxAdditionalLights.

void setRenderQualitySettings(const RenderQualitySettings &settings)

Apply explicit viewer-quality settings at runtime.

Besides storing (and clamping) the settings, this re-derives renderer state from them: background color, fog density, gamma, depth of field, the main light (type reset to directional, direction, colors, shadow resolution and parameters), the shadow box and center offset, and texture filtering of loaded textures. It also clears all additional lights and, when RenderQualitySettings::addViewerFillLights is set, adds the built-in fill and rim lights. The active preset becomes Custom. With weather enabled the settings become the base that weather is applied on.

Parameters:

settings – Settings to apply. Throws std::invalid_argument for an unknown temporal AA method, a non-finite jitter scale, a current weight outside [0.02, 1] or a sharpness outside [0, 1].

ShaderWarmupDiagnostics shaderWarmupDiagnostics() const

Return startup shader compile/warmup diagnostics for built-in RayRai programs.

RayRai registers all built-in shader programs during construction and compiles optional shaders lazily on first use. This exposes the measured compile/link cost and linked program count so startup and first-use stalls can be tracked.

Returns:

Warmup diagnostics (queries GL program state; GL context required).

std::vector<std::string> linkedShaderNames() const

Names of every shader program currently linked, sorted alphabetically. Useful for diagnostics and for callers that want to record the “hot set” of shaders an application actually uses so a future run can pre-warm only those.

Returns:

Sorted program names.

long long warmupNextShader(bool &done)

Compile one not-yet-compiled built-in shader program, if any.

Returns the number of milliseconds spent compiling (0 if no work was done). The output flag done is set to true when every registered program has been compiled at least once. Iterates all registered programs — most of which an application typically doesn’t use; prefer compileShaderByName to pre-warm just the heavy shaders your active scene actually exercises. Must be called on the thread that owns the GL context.

Parameters:

done – [out] Set to true when nothing was left to compile, false otherwise.

Returns:

Milliseconds spent compiling. Throws std::runtime_error when a shader fails.

long long compileShaderByName(const std::string &name)

Compile a specific built-in shader by name if not already linked. Returns the milliseconds spent compiling (0 if already linked or unknown name). Lets the application warm just the shaders it knows will be needed — e.g. pbrMeshHigh (the high-fidelity PBR mesh program) is typically the dominant cost for content rendering, so pre-warming only that one avoids most of the visible “freeze” on the first content frame without paying for unused shader variants. Must be called on the thread that owns the GL context.

Parameters:

name – Built-in program name (see linkedShaderNames()).

Returns:

Milliseconds spent compiling. Throws std::runtime_error when the shader fails.

MaterialTextureBudgetRecommendation recommendMaterialTextureBudget(size_t budgetBytes = 0) const

Build a non-mutating material texture memory fallback recommendation.

If budgetBytes is zero, a conservative preset-aware default is used. The recommendation only changes quality settings that reduce texture sampling/setup cost; it does not unload existing textures or alter sensor behavior. Texture sizes are queried from GL, so call it with this renderer’s GL context current.

Parameters:

budgetBytes – Texture memory budget in bytes; 0 selects the preset default.

Returns:

Recommendation; apply recommendedSettings yourself if desired.

Public Static Functions

static unsigned int loadTextureWithTiling(const char *path, bool useSrgbFormat = false)

Load an image file into an OpenGL texture with repeat tiling.

The texture gets GL_REPEAT wrapping, mipmaps, and the process-wide defaults from setDefaultTextureFilteringQuality(). Results are cached per thread and per GL context by (path, sRGB flag), so repeated calls return the same id; a failed load is cached as 0 too. Requires a current GL context.

Parameters:

  • path – Path to an image file supported by stb_image.

  • useSrgbFormat – If true, RGB/RGBA textures are uploaded as sRGB color textures. Use true for albedo/emissive color maps and false for data maps such as normal, metallic-roughness, AO, depth, and masks.

Returns:

OpenGL texture id, or 0 on failure.

static unsigned int updateSingleChannelTexture(unsigned int existingTextureId, int width, int height, const unsigned char *data)

Create or update a single-channel R8 2D texture from raw pixel data.

Used for terrain splat control maps. Pass existingTextureId 0 to allocate a new texture, otherwise the existing texture is updated in place (and reallocated if the dimensions differ). New textures use linear filtering and clamp-to-edge wrapping. Requires a current GL context.

Parameters:

  • existingTextureId – Texture to update, or 0 (or a deleted id) to create one.

  • width – Width in pixels; must be positive.

  • height – Height in pixels; must be positive.

  • data – width * height tightly packed bytes; must not be null.

Returns:

The texture id (new or reused), or 0 on invalid input.

static unsigned int createHdrIrradianceCubemap(const char *path, int faceSize = 32, int sampleCount = 256)

Generate a diffuse irradiance cubemap from a Radiance .hdr equirectangular environment.

This is CPU-side cosine-hemisphere integration intended for High/Ultra PBR setup. Creation is explicit so Fast/Balanced RL rendering does not pay the cost.

Parameters:

  • path – Path to a .hdr image supported by stb_image.

  • faceSize – Irradiance cubemap face size in pixels.

  • sampleCount – Number of hemisphere samples per texel.

Returns:

OpenGL cubemap id, or 0 on failure.

static unsigned int createHdrPrefilteredEnvironmentCubemap(const char *path, int faceSize = 128, int mipLevels = 5, int sampleCount = 256)

Generate a prefiltered specular environment cubemap from a Radiance .hdr equirectangular environment.

Mip level 0 is sharp and higher mip levels are GGX-prefiltered with increasing roughness. Use this as Material::prefilteredEnvironmentMap together with createSplitSumBrdfLut().

Parameters:

  • path – Path to a .hdr image supported by stb_image.

  • faceSize – Base cubemap face size in pixels.

  • mipLevels – Number of mip levels to allocate and integrate.

  • sampleCount – Number of GGX samples per texel.

Returns:

OpenGL cubemap id, or 0 on failure.

static unsigned int createSplitSumBrdfLut(int size = 256, int sampleCount = 512)

Create a numerically integrated split-sum BRDF LUT.

Use this as Material::brdfLut for High/Ultra PBR. Creation is explicit so Fast/Balance paths do not pay for it. The result is an RG16F texture (x = N.V, y = roughness).

Parameters:

  • size – LUT width and height in texels.

  • sampleCount – GGX samples per texel.

Returns:

OpenGL texture id owned by the caller, or 0 if either argument is not positive.

static void setTextureAnisotropy(unsigned int target, unsigned int textureId, float requestedLevel)

Apply anisotropic filtering to an existing 2D or cubemap texture if supported.

Parameters:

  • target – Texture target such as GL_TEXTURE_2D or GL_TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP.

  • textureId – OpenGL texture id.

  • requestedLevel – Requested anisotropy level. Values <= 1 leave the texture unchanged.

static void setTextureFilteringQuality(unsigned int target, unsigned int textureId, float anisotropy, float mipLodBias)

Apply minification quality controls to an existing texture.

Positive mip LOD bias prefers blurrier mips and reduces distant texture shimmer. Negative values sharpen but can alias, so RayRai clamps the bias to [-1, 2].

Parameters:

  • target – Texture target such as GL_TEXTURE_2D.

  • textureId – OpenGL texture id; 0 is ignored.

  • anisotropy – Requested anisotropy, see setTextureAnisotropy().

  • mipLodBias – Mip LOD bias, clamped to [-1, 2].

static void setDefaultTextureFilteringQuality(float anisotropy, float mipLodBias)

Set process-wide filtering defaults used by future loadTextureWithTiling() calls.

Parameters:

  • anisotropy – Default anisotropy, clamped to [1, 16].

  • mipLodBias – Default mip LOD bias, clamped to [-1, 2].

static void getDefaultTextureFilteringQuality(float &anisotropy, float &mipLodBias)

Read process-wide filtering defaults used by future loadTextureWithTiling() calls.

Parameters:

  • anisotropy – [out] Default anisotropy.

  • mipLodBias – [out] Default mip LOD bias.

static void setTextureSamplerState(unsigned int target, unsigned int textureId, int wrapS, int wrapT, int minFilter, int magFilter)

Apply sampler wrap/filter state to an existing texture.

Parameters:

  • target – Texture target such as GL_TEXTURE_2D.

  • textureId – OpenGL texture id; 0 is ignored.

  • wrapS – GL wrap mode for S (e.g. GL_REPEAT).

  • wrapT – GL wrap mode for T.

  • minFilter – GL minification filter.

  • magFilter – GL magnification filter.

static inline unsigned int loadDataTextureWithTiling(const char *path)

static void createOffscreenGlContext(SDL_Window *&window, SDL_GLContext &glContext, const char *title = "rayrai_offscreen")

Create a hidden SDL window and an offscreen OpenGL context.

If the calling thread already has a current SDL OpenGL context, the new context joins its share group. This lets worker renderers reuse immutable untextured mesh buffers while retaining context-local VAOs and render targets. With no current context, an independent root context is created. Initializes SDL video if needed and requests an OpenGL 4.3 core context, falling back to 3.3. The new context is left current on the calling thread. Aborts (RSFATAL) when the window or context cannot be created. The caller owns both handles (SDL_GL_DeleteContext / SDL_DestroyWindow).

Parameters:

  • window – Output pointer for the created SDL window.

  • glContext – Output handle for the OpenGL context.

  • title – Window title for the hidden SDL window.

static void makeOffscreenContextCurrent(SDL_Window *window, SDL_GLContext glContext)

Make an existing offscreen context current and update glbinding.

Also resets rayrai’s per-context binding caches. Aborts (RSFATAL) on a null argument or when SDL cannot make the context current.

Parameters:

  • window – SDL window owning the OpenGL context.

  • glContext – OpenGL context to make current.

static void detachOffscreenGlContext(SDL_Window *window)

Detach the GL context currently bound to window on this thread.

createOffscreenGlContext leaves the context it made current on the calling thread, so a context created on the main thread has to be released before a worker can adopt it with makeOffscreenContextCurrent — a context is current on at most one thread at a time. Safe to call with no context current.

Parameters:

window – SDL window whose context should be released; nullptr is a no-op.

static void prewarmShadersForCurrentContext(ThreadingMode threadingMode = ThreadingMode::MultiThread, std::string shaderBinaryCacheDirectory = std::string{})

Compile every built-in shader using the GL context currently bound to the calling thread, populating the on-disk binary cache.

Intended for parallel RL workflows: spawn a background thread that holds its own offscreen GL context, call this once, and worker threads that later construct RayraiWindow instances will find the heavy shaders already in the cache (or briefly block on the per-shader compile mutex for any program this thread is still finishing).

Net effect across a process: each shader’s GLSL→binary compile runs exactly once, regardless of how many worker threads concurrently construct RayraiWindows.

Pre-conditions: the caller’s thread has made a valid offscreen GL context current. Post-condition: the temporary RayraiWindow used for compilation is destroyed before this returns; the caller’s context is left current. The caller is responsible for the surrounding SDL_GL_MakeCurrent(nullptr) / SDL_GL_DeleteContext / thread join.

Side effect: the temporary renderer re-applies the process-wide shader settings (one compile thread, binary cache enabled at shaderBinaryCacheDirectory, cache logging off), like any constructor.

Parameters:

  • threadingMode – Must match the mode used by the worker threads that will eventually construct their own RayraiWindows. Defaults to MultiThread since prewarming only makes sense when other threads will also render.

  • shaderBinaryCacheDirectory – Optional explicit cache directory. Empty selects the default per-user cache directory (see the RayraiWindow constructor).

face – Face index in GL order (+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z), clamped to [0, 5].

The face’s camera basis.

Parse the reflection-probe sidecar that belongs to a scene file (CPU only).

Sidecar lookup (shared by all sidecar loaders): if sceneFile itself ends in .json it is used; otherwise <sceneFile>.rayrai_probes.json, then <dir>/<stem>.rayrai_probes.json. The first existing file wins. Nothing is captured; use the returned entries with captureFilteredReflectionProbe().

  • loadedSidecarPath – [out] Optional path of the file that was read (empty if none).

Returns:

Parsed probes; empty when no sidecar exists or it has no probes array.

static DynamicQualityRecommendation recommendDynamicQuality(const RenderQualitySettings &settings, RenderQualityPreset preset, const std::vector<RenderPassTiming> &timings)

Build a sensor-safe dynamic-quality recommendation from explicit GPU pass timings.

This does not mutate renderer state. It is intended for Fast/Balanced viewer loops that explicitly opt into adaptive render scale or static shadow updates after measuring GPU cost. High/Ultra recommendations never change settings. Otherwise, when the summed GPU time exceeds the preset budget, shadow-bound frames stop per-frame shadow updates, fill-bound frames lower viewerRenderScale by 15 % (not below 0.6 for Fast, 0.75 otherwise), and post-process-bound frames reduce bloom/AO/indirect-lighting cost.

Parameters:

  • settings – Current settings.

  • preset – Preset that selects the budget (see DynamicQualityRecommendation::targetFrameMs).

  • timings – Pass timings, e.g. from captureRenderPassTimings().

Returns:

Recommendation.

static RgbaLuminanceMetrics analyzeRgbaLuminance(const std::vector<unsigned char> &rgba, int width, int height)

Analyze display-space luminance and saturation from an RGBA8 capture.

This is intended for exposure/tone-map diagnostics and image regression tests. It does not render or read from OpenGL; callers pass already captured RGBA8 pixels.

Parameters:

  • rgba – RGBA8 pixels (alpha ignored); at most width * height pixels are read.

  • width – Image width in pixels.

  • height – Image height in pixels.

Returns:

Metrics; zero-filled for empty or invalid input.

static ExposureRecommendation recommendExposure(const RgbaLuminanceMetrics &metrics, double currentExposure = 1.0, double targetMedianLuminance = 0.45, double targetP95Luminance = 0.90, double minExposure = 0.125, double maxExposure = 8.0)

Build a bounded exposure recommendation from display-space luminance metrics.

This does not mutate renderer state. It is intended for explicit viewer calibration, quality-comparison reports, and offline screenshot tooling. Sensor renders should only apply the result if the caller explicitly opts into viewer-style postprocessing.

Highlights take priority: clipping (> 1 % channels) or p95 above target scales the exposure down to the p95 target; otherwise midtones below 70 % / above 135 % of the median target are corrected toward it without pushing p95 past its target.

Parameters:

  • metrics – Metrics of an image rendered at currentExposure.

  • currentExposure – Exposure used for that image; must be positive.

  • targetMedianLuminance – Desired median display luminance.

  • targetP95Luminance – Desired 95th percentile display luminance.

  • minExposure – Lower clamp for the result; must be positive.

  • maxExposure – Upper clamp for the result.

Returns:

Recommendation; valid is false for invalid input.

static double smoothExposure(double currentExposure, double targetExposure, double deltaSeconds, double brightenRate = 1.2, double darkenRate = 3.0, double minExposure = 0.125, double maxExposure = 8.0)

Smooth an explicitly chosen exposure target over time.

This helper is stateless and does not mutate renderer settings. Use a larger darken rate than brighten rate to adapt quickly away from clipping while avoiding flicker when lifting dark scenes. Computes current + (target - current) * (1 - exp(-rate * dt)) with both exposures clamped to [minExposure, maxExposure].

Parameters:

  • currentExposure – Current exposure.

  • targetExposure – Desired exposure.

  • deltaSeconds – Elapsed time in seconds.

  • brightenRate – Rate (1/s) used when the target is brighter.

  • darkenRate – Rate (1/s) used when the target is darker.

  • minExposure – Lower exposure bound.

  • maxExposure – Upper exposure bound.

Returns:

New exposure; the clamped current exposure when any input is invalid.

struct RenderOverrides

Override shaders and rendering toggles when using external cameras.

For Camera-based external renders, drawVisualizationObjects and drawPointClouds enable only custom visuals, instanced visuals, and point clouds marked VisualCategory::Detectable. Non-detectable helper geometry remains visible in the normal interactive viewer but is skipped by these capture paths. The RaiSim RGB/depth sensor-camera overloads disable custom visualization objects and point clouds entirely, regardless of these toggles.

class VisualMeshBuilder

Fluent builder for addVisualMesh.

Collects scale/position/orientation/material and flags up front; add() creates the visual via the corresponding addVisualMesh overload, then applies the deferred state via the existing setters and returns the shared_ptr<Visuals>. Setters on the returned visual still work for runtime mutations after creation.

Example: 

auto v = renderer.makeVisualMesh("rusty", path)
  .scale({1.0, 1.0, 1.0})
  .position({0.0, 0.0, 0.5})
  .orientation(glm::angleAxis(0.4f, glm::vec3{0, 0, 1}))
  .twoSided(true)
  .pickable(true)
  .castsShadows(true)
  .material(rusty)
  .pbrEnvironment(env)
  .add();

Only options that were set are applied. The builder stores a raw pointer to the renderer, which must outlive it.

class Camera

Camera for offscreen rendering and interaction.

The camera owns its render targets (scene color/depth, post-process, linear depth, and picking). It can be driven by user input or by raisim sensor parameters.

Public Functions

explicit Camera(glm::vec3 position = glm::vec3(5.0f, 4.0f, 5.0f), glm::vec3 up = glm::vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f), float yaw = -135.0f, float pitch = -30.0f)

Construct a camera with a position, up vector, and yaw/pitch.

Does not allocate GL resources. The view direction is (cos(yaw)cos(pitch), sin(yaw)cos(pitch), sin(pitch)), i.e. yaw is measured about +Z from +X and pitch upward from the XY plane (Z-up world).

Parameters:

  • position – Camera position in world coordinates.

  • up – World up vector (stored in worldUp).

  • yaw – Initial yaw angle in degrees.

  • pitch – Initial pitch angle in degrees.

void mouseDelta(float yawOffset, float pitchOffset)

Apply mouse delta to yaw/pitch or pan in orthographic mode.

Perspective: yaw -= yawOffset, pitch += pitchOffset (pitch clamped to +-89 deg). Orthographic: pans the position by 0.05 m per unit. Call update() afterwards to refresh the direction vectors.

Parameters:

  • pitchOffset – Delta pitch in degrees (screen-space delta).

void moveForward(float steps)

Move forward/backward or zoom in orthographic mode.

Free perspective camera: moves steps metres along front. Orthographic: scales orthoScale by 0.9^steps (min 0.1), so positive zooms in. Orbiting a target or with a fixed distance: scales the orbit distance by 1.2^steps (min 0.05 m), so positive steps move away from the target.

Parameters:

steps – Signed step count (e.g. mouse-wheel delta).

void setSceneMsaaSamples(int samples)

Set scene-color MSAA samples for future scene FBO rendering.

Values <= 1 disable MSAA. The resolved color/depth are still written into the existing single-sample texture targets so postprocessing and readback APIs keep working.

Parameters:

samples – Requested sample count; values above 1 are clamped to [2, GL_MAX_SAMPLES].

void setSceneMsaaSamples(int samples, bool keepAllocation)

Same as setSceneMsaaSamples(), optionally keeping an existing multisampled target.

With keepAllocation, disabling MSAA keeps the multisampled renderbuffers so re-enabling the same sample count reuses them instead of reallocating. Every scene render clears the target before drawing, so reuse cannot change the image. A later call without keepAllocation that leaves MSAA disabled releases the kept target.

Parameters:

  • samples – Requested sample count, as in the single-argument overload.

  • keepAllocation – Keep the multisampled renderbuffers when disabling MSAA.

void updateAutoExposure(float targetKey, float speed, float minFactor, float maxFactor)

Sample mean scene-color luma and lerp the auto-exposure factor.

Every 4th call issues an asynchronous PBO readback of the smallest mip of the post-process (or scene) color; a completed earlier readback, if any, yields the mean luma, and autoExposureFactor_ is smoothed toward targetKey / mean. Never blocks: without a ready sample the factor is unchanged. Should be called once per frame, after post-process completes. The stored factor is then applied to the next frame’s pbrExposure.

Parameters:

  • targetKey – Desired mean luma (approximately linear, 0..1).

  • speed – Lerp factor per update, clamped to [0, 1].

  • minFactor – Lower clamp of the exposure factor.

  • maxFactor – Upper clamp of the exposure factor.

Camera pose and view parameters (public for quick access).

Distances are in world units (typically metres). Angles in degrees unless the field name ends in Rad. nearPlane/farPlane and zNear/zFar are overlapping pairs from earlier API revisions: they are not aliases; the projection uses the wider of the two ranges (see getProjectionClipRange()), so with the default zNear of 0.01 raising only nearPlane has no effect. class RayraiGlobalAsset

A caching asset manager for 3D models and primitive meshes.

This class loads models on demand and keeps them in memory as long as they are being used. Once all references to a model are released, its memory can be reclaimed. It also owns reusable meshes for primitives such as cubes, spheres, cylinders, and capsules.

Returned mesh lists are shared: every caller that requests the same asset gets the same std::shared_ptr, so mutating a mesh’s material affects all users. Not thread-safe; use it from the thread that owns the GL context.

Public Functions

RayraiGlobalAsset()

Construct the asset cache and generate primitive meshes.

Requires a current OpenGL context (primitive meshes are uploaded here, or reused from another context in the same share group).

~RayraiGlobalAsset()

Destroy the asset cache.

std::shared_ptr<std::vector<std::shared_ptr<OpenGLMesh>>> getMeshes(const std::string &name)

Retrieves a model’s meshes by its asset name (usually file path).

Assets are keyed by canonical path, so different spellings of the same file share one mesh list. With async loading enabled (the default; USD files always load synchronously) a new file returns an empty list at once that is filled in place by a later pollAsyncLoads(); if that import fails the list stays empty. The cache holds only weak references. Requires a current GL context for synchronous loads.

Parameters:

name – The unique identifier for the asset, typically the file path.

Returns:

Shared mesh list (possibly still empty while loading), or nullptr if the path does not exist or a synchronous load fails.

void forgetChangedModelFiles()

Forget every cached model file whose sources changed since it was read.

A model’s sources are its file and every file its import read (glTF buffers, an OBJ material library, …). A changed one makes the next getMeshes() read the model again, even while visuals still hold the meshes read before. RayraiWindow::swapWorld() calls this, so a rebuilt scene shows edited files.

inline void releaseRecentlyReadModels()

Release the models read from files since the last call.

A model read from a file stays referenced until this is called, so every visual created in the same frame shares one read, even when a visual keeps only meshes derived from it (instanced foliage keeps its partitioned meshes, and a terrain foliage layer adds one visual per chunk). RayraiWindow calls this at the end of each update(), renderWithExternalCamera(), and depth-only render.

Returns:

True when future mesh file imports start on a worker thread.

Visuals and geometry

class Visuals

Renderable visual object not owned by raisim::World.

Visuals encapsulate geometry, transform, and appearance for custom renderable shapes or meshes.

The world transform is position, then orientation, then a per-axis scale applied in the mesh’s local frame (Z-up world, quaternions passed as wxyz). Built-in primitives and file meshes come from RayraiGlobalAsset and are shared with other visuals; per-visual appearance belongs in the color, material override/remap/overlay and flags below rather than in the shared meshes. Setters only change state (and renderRevision()); GL work happens when the renderer draws, so drawing requires a current GL context.

Material queries

Internal: renderer pass-selection queries over the visual’s draw materials (override, remaps and overlay included). Each mirrors the RaisimObject query of the same name.

inline void setPbrEnvironment(unsigned int environmentMap, unsigned int brdfLut = 0, float strength = 1.0f)

Apply an image-based lighting environment to all PBR submeshes.

Same as the split overload with no irradiance or prefiltered map.

Parameters:

  • environmentMap – GL cubemap id (0 clears).

  • brdfLut – Split-sum BRDF LUT texture id, or 0.

  • strength – Environment strength (Material::environmentMapStrength).

inline void setPbrEnvironment(unsigned int environmentMap, unsigned int irradianceMap, unsigned int prefilteredEnvironmentMap, unsigned int brdfLut, float strength = 1.0f, bool boxProjection = false, const glm::vec3 &probePosition = glm::vec3(0.0f), const glm::vec3 &boxMin = glm::vec3(0.0f), const glm::vec3 &boxMax = glm::vec3(0.0f))

Apply split image-based lighting maps to all PBR submeshes.

This mirrors the real-time IBL layout used by engines such as Filament: a display/environment cubemap, diffuse irradiance, prefiltered specular radiance, and a split-sum BRDF LUT. Supplying the full set gives whole-scene imported visuals the same high-fidelity path used by hand-built PBR meshes.

The ids are written into the materials of this visual’s meshes (and LOD meshes), material override, remaps and overlay, skipping materials that look like plain simple-shaded ones; a non-zero cubemap also switches those materials to Type::PBR. Mesh materials are edited in place, so other visuals sharing the same cached meshes see the change. Texture ids are not owned.

Parameters:

  • environmentMap – Radiance/display cubemap id.

  • irradianceMap – Diffuse irradiance cubemap id, or 0.

  • prefilteredEnvironmentMap – Prefiltered specular cubemap id, or 0.

  • brdfLut – Split-sum BRDF LUT texture id, or 0.

  • strength – Environment strength (capped further for heightmap terrain).

  • boxProjection – Enable box-projected (parallax-corrected) reflections.

  • probePosition – Probe capture position in world coordinates.

  • boxMin – World-space minimum corner of the projection box.

  • boxMax – World-space maximum corner of the projection box.

inline void setPbrEnvironment(const PbrEnvironment &env)

Apply a PbrEnvironment bundle to all PBR submeshes.

Convenience overload that unpacks the four texture handles and the strength scalar from a single struct, eliminating the need for callers to juggle four raw GL ids in parallel.

Parameters:

env – Environment bundle (also carries the box-projection settings).

inline void setCategory(VisualCategory category)

Set the render category used by capture/detection filters.

The category controls whether this user-created visual is included when a rayrai pass excludes non-detectable visualization objects, such as external camera scene-color renders, capture paths that reuse external-camera rendering, or picking/shadow candidate policies that request detectable custom visuals. The normal interactive viewer includes both categories by default.

This is render metadata only; it does not create collision, physics behavior, or a semantic label. New Visuals default to VisualCategory::NotDetectable.

void setMaterialOverride(std::shared_ptr<Material> material)

Override the visual’s draw material with a shared instance.

Ownership. The same shared_ptr<Material> may be held by any number of other visuals — setMaterialOverride does not deep-copy. Mutating the pointed-to material from any holder is observed by every visual that shares it. If you want an in-place edit that affects only this visual, call the const Material& overload (which copies into a new shared instance) or grab a fresh copy via *materialOverride() and push it back through setMaterialOverride(Material{...}).

The override replaces the material of every submesh (and takes precedence over material remaps); the meshes’ own OpenGLMesh::textures are then ignored.

Parameters:

material – Material to draw with; null clears the override.

void setMaterialOverride(const Material &material)

Override the visual’s draw material with a private copy.

Copies material into a freshly allocated shared instance so later mutations affect only this visual. Prefer this overload when the material is going to be tweaked per-visual.

Parameters:

material – Material to copy.

Draw submeshes back-to-front relative to a camera position.

This is intended for transparent mesh visuals. It is more expensive than draw(), so rayrai only uses it on the transparent visual path. Submeshes are ordered by material render priority, then by distance (farthest first). Uses the source mesh (no LOD) and applies the visibility-range alpha.

  • viewPos – Camera position in world coordinates.

  • mode – Material filter.
