class InstancedVisuals

Many copies of one shape or mesh drawn with GPU instancing.

Each instance has a position, wxyz orientation, scale and a color weight that blends between the two batch colors (getColor1(), getColor2()) (mix(color1, color2, weight)). Appearance (colors, category, shadow flag) is shared by the whole batch. Instance edits are cheap CPU updates; the GPU instance buffer is refreshed lazily on the next draw, which requires a current GL context. Mesh batches may get automatic LODs prepared on a worker thread; such a batch draws nothing until that preparation has finished (see pollAsyncMeshPreparation()). Batches that look like foliage (alpha-masked or foliage materials, or a foliage-like file name) also enable shadow LOD, cluster culling and impostors by default.

Draw-path diagnostics

Internal: results of the most recent draw, for tests and renderer diagnostics.

inline void setCategory(VisualCategory category)

Set the render category used by capture/detection filters.

The category is shared by all instances in this batch. It controls whether the instanced visual is included when a rayrai pass excludes non-detectable visualization objects, such as external camera scene-color renders, capture paths that reuse external-camera rendering, or picking/shadow candidate policies that request detectable custom visuals. The normal interactive viewer includes both categories by default.

This is render metadata only; it does not create collision, physics behavior, or per-instance semantic labels. New InstancedVisuals default to VisualCategory::NotDetectable.

See also

VisualCategory

Parameters:

category – New render category for the whole instanced batch.

void setProjectedLodPolicy(bool enabled, float minProjectedRadiusPixels = 2.0f, size_t maxStride = 8)

Enable camera-projected LOD for instanced visuals.

When enabled, the renderer increases the effective draw stride for far-away instances whose approximate per-instance radius projects below minProjectedRadiusPixels. The explicit rendered stride remains a lower bound, so user-requested LOD is preserved. Requires a camera-aware draw() overload (a positive viewport height).

Parameters:

  • enabled – Enable the policy.

  • minProjectedRadiusPixels – Target projected instance radius in pixels (min 0.25).

  • maxStride – Largest stride the policy may choose (min 1).

void setPreparedMeshLods(std::span<const std::shared_ptr<std::vector<std::shared_ptr<OpenGLMesh>>>> levels)

Install six authored LOD levels; source geometry remains level zero. Mesh lists may have different material/part counts. Every mesh must carry a finite nonnegative generatedLodRelativeError for projected selection. Authored levels use opaque/masked single-pass ordinary materials. Disabling automatic LODs clears this chain; reinstall it to re-enable these authored levels.

void configureGrassPatch(float patchWidth, float patchDepth, float densityPerSquareMeter, size_t drawBudget, float maxDrawDistance, float lodFadeStartDistance, float lodFadeEndDistance, uint32_t seed, float bladeRootHeight = 0.0f, float bladeTipHeight = 1.0f, float windStrength = 1.0f, float stiffness = 0.35f, float flutterWeight = 0.15f)

Mark this instanced visual as a grass patch and configure bounded draw/wind metadata.

Instances are still authored through addInstance()/resize() so callers keep full control over density masks and scatter placement. This method wires the batch into the generic foliage wind shader path, projected LOD, and render diagnostics.

Also caps drawn instances at drawBudget and enables projected LOD, shadow foliage LOD and hierarchical cluster culling with fixed defaults. Width, depth, density and seed are recorded for diagnostics only.

Parameters:

  • patchWidth – Patch width (m).

  • patchDepth – Patch depth (m).

  • densityPerSquareMeter – Blade density.

  • drawBudget – Maximum drawn instances (0 = unlimited).

  • maxDrawDistance – View depth at which blades have faded out (m); 0 = no limit.

  • lodFadeStartDistance – View depth where blades start fading (m).

  • lodFadeEndDistance – View depth where that fade ends (m).

  • seed – Scatter seed (metadata).

  • bladeRootHeight – Local height below which blades do not bend.

  • bladeTipHeight – Local height of full bend.

  • windStrength – Wind bend strength (>= 0).

  • stiffness – Bend stiffness, clamped to [0, 1].

  • flutterWeight – High-frequency flutter weight (>= 0).

Configure conservative BVH/quadtree-style foliage cluster culling.

Cluster culling only removes instances whose cluster bounds are outside the current view/shadow frustum. It does not reduce authored instance count or change material/mesh quality.

class OpenGLMesh : public std::enable_shared_from_this<OpenGLMesh>

Simple OpenGL mesh with indexed geometry and optional textures.

Keeps a CPU copy of the geometry plus a context-local VAO and (possibly shared) VBO/EBO. Constructors and every update/draw method require a current OpenGL context, except createCpuGeometry() and prepareGeometryAttributes(). Texture ids referenced by textures and material are not owned. Meshes are usually held by std::shared_ptr and may be shared between objects (see RayraiGlobalAsset), so material edits on a shared mesh affect every user. Non-copyable and non-movable.

Public Types

enum class RenderMode

Material filter applied by draw(); used to split a scene into shader passes.

Values:

enumerator All

Draw regardless of shading type, using the simple-shader uniform path.

enumerator SimpleOnly

Draw only meshes that do not use PBR shading.

enumerator PbrOnly

Draw only PBR meshes (all passes).

enumerator PbrNonTransmissiveOnly

PBR passes whose material is not transmissive.

enumerator PbrTransmissiveOnly

PBR passes whose material is transmissive (glass path).

enum class PrimitiveTopology

GL primitive used to interpret the index buffer.

Values:

enumerator Triangles

GL_TRIANGLES.

enumerator Lines

GL_LINES (width from setLineWidth()).

enumerator Points

GL_POINTS (size from setPointSize()).

Public Functions

bool drawsInMode(RenderMode mode, const raisin::Material *materialOverride) const

Whether draw() with the same arguments would rasterize anything. It mirrors the mode and transmission filters draw() applies, including the nextPass chain, so a caller can skip a program bind and a whole submission instead of paying for a draw that returns immediately.

Parameters:

  • materialOverride – Material to test instead of material, or nullptr.

Returns:

Missing tangents are generated and an empty TexCoords2 set is filled from TexCoords. The material type is TEXTURED when textures is non-empty, else SIMPLE_COLOR. GPU indices stay 32-bit (see createWithCompactIndices()).

void draw(const Shader &shader) const

Draw the mesh using the provided shader.

Same as draw(shader, RenderMode::All). The shader is not bound here and must already be in use; the model matrix and objectColor are the caller’s responsibility. Material depth/stencil/blend/cull state is applied around the draw call.

Parameters:

void draw(const Shader &shader, RenderMode mode, const raisin::Material *materialOverride = nullptr) const

Draw the mesh if it matches the requested material render mode.

Non-PBR modes set the simple-shader material uniforms and bind the diffuse, specular and normal maps to units 0, 1 and 2 (white fallback when absent). PBR modes apply the full material (Material::applyTo()) and also draw its next-pass chain. The shader must already be in use.

Parameters:

  • shader – Shader with expected material uniforms.

  • mode – Material filter for multi-pass rendering.

  • materialOverride – Optional material to use instead of the mesh material (the mesh’s textures are then ignored).

unsigned int instancedVaoForBuffer(unsigned int instanceBuffer) const

Return a VAO whose base mesh attributes plus instance attributes use instanceBuffer.

The instance buffer holds one 80-byte record per instance: a column-major mat4 model matrix (attributes 3-6) followed by a vec4 color (attribute 7). VAOs are created on first use and cached per buffer; call releaseInstancedVaoForBuffer() before deleting the buffer.

Parameters:

instanceBuffer – GL array buffer with instance records; 0 returns 0.

Returns:

VAO id owned by this mesh, or 0 on failure.

static std::shared_ptr<OpenGLMesh> createIndexedRangeView(std::shared_ptr<const OpenGLMesh> owner, const std::vector<Vertex> &localVertices, const std::vector<unsigned int> &localIndices, size_t firstIndex, int baseVertex, const raisin::Material &viewMaterial, const glm::vec4 &viewBaseColor, const std::string &debugName = {})

Create a CPU-metadata view into owner's indexed GPU buffers.

The returned mesh has its own material/CPU geometry metadata but shares owner's VAO/EBO/VBO and draws the requested index range. It does not own or delete the shared GL handles, and holds a shared_ptr to owner so the borrowed GL handles cannot dangle.

Taking the owner as an explicit std::shared_ptr makes shared ownership a compile-time requirement (no shared_from_this/bad_weak_ptr fallback that could silently return a non-owning view), and the view is built without any throwaway GL upload — it never allocates its own VAO/VBO/EBO. Returns null if owner is null.

Parameters:

  • owner – Mesh whose GPU buffers are borrowed.

  • localVertices – CPU vertices for this view (bounds/diagnostics only).

  • localIndices – CPU indices for this view; their count is the draw count.

  • firstIndex – Offset, in indices, into owner's index buffer.

  • baseVertex – Value added to each index when drawing.

  • viewMaterial – Material of the view.

  • viewBaseColor – Base color of the view.

  • debugName – Diagnostics name; empty inherits owner's.

Returns:

The view, or nullptr.

static std::shared_ptr<OpenGLMesh> createSharedGpuGeometryView(const std::shared_ptr<const OpenGLMesh> &owner)

Create a context-local mesh wrapper that reuses another mesh’s GPU buffers.

Buffer objects and textures are shared by OpenGL context share groups, while vertex array objects are context-local. This factory copies the CPU/material metadata, retains the shared VBO/EBO allocation, and creates a VAO in the caller’s current context.

Parameters:

owner – Source mesh; its buffers must be visible in the current context.

Returns:

The view, or nullptr if owner is null, has no shareable buffers, or is not visible from the current context.

class PointCloud

Simple point cloud renderer.

Stores positions and colors on the CPU; nothing reaches the GPU until one of the update methods is called. GL buffers are created lazily on the first upload and released in the destructor, so construction needs no GL context but every update/draw call and the destructor (once uploaded) do.

Public Functions

Construct an empty point cloud.

Destroy the point cloud and release GPU resources.

inline void setCategory(VisualCategory category)

Set the render category used by capture/detection filters.

Point clouds are visible in the normal interactive viewer regardless of this category. External-camera and generated-capture passes can request only detectable point clouds, in which case clouds left as VisualCategory::NotDetectable are skipped. This lets debug lidar traces, helper samples, and temporary overlays remain visible to a human operator without appearing in external-camera or generated capture images.

This is render metadata only; it does not create collision, physics behavior, or semantic labels. New PointCloud instances default to VisualCategory::NotDetectable.

See also

VisualCategory

category – New render category.

enum class raisin::VisualCategory

Render-category flag for user-created visuals and point clouds.

VisualCategory is render metadata. Rayrai uses it when a render policy asks for only capture/detection-visible helper geometry, for example external camera renders, capture paths that reuse external-camera rendering, detectable-only point-cloud rendering, and picking or shadow candidate passes that explicitly require detectable visualization objects.

This flag does not create a physics body, collision shape, dynamics object, or semantic label, and it does not hide an object from the normal interactive viewer. User-created Visuals, InstancedVisuals, PointCloud, and helpers built on top of Visuals default to NotDetectable so debug overlays, camera frustums, axes, labels, and other viewer-only aids do not contaminate external-camera or generated capture images.

Set a visual to Detectable when it should be included in those capture/detection render passes. RaiSim world objects are not controlled by this enum; they follow their own wrapper visibility and the active render pass policy. The RaiSim RGB/depth sensor-camera overloads intentionally disable custom visualization objects and point clouds regardless of this flag.

Values:

enumerator NotDetectable

Viewer-only by default; excluded from detectable-only render passes.

enumerator Detectable

Included when a rayrai render policy asks for detectable custom visuals.

Rendering and materials

class Light

Simple light with optional shadow map support.

Supports all LightType models and owns the shadow-map framebuffer and depth textures used by the renderer. GL resources are created lazily by the shadow pre-pass methods (which need a current OpenGL context) and released in the destructor when the creating context is current; otherwise the ids are dropped without deletion. Non-copyable and non-movable.

Color terms

Linear RGB multipliers (not clamped; values above 1 brighten). The ambient term is added without distance attenuation.

glm::vec3 ambient

Constant term added regardless of surface orientation.

glm::vec3 diffuse

Lambertian term.

glm::vec3 specular

Highlight term.

Attenuation

Inverse-quadratic falloff for point, spot and area lights: intensity / (constant + linear*r + quadratic*r^2) where r is in metres (never less than radius). Ignored for directional lights. Use setRange() for a more ergonomic alternative.

float constant

Constant denominator term.

float linear

Coefficient of r (1/m).

float quadratic

Coefficient of r^2 (1/m^2).

Projector (light cookie)

Optional 2D texture that tints the light; not applied to point lights.

unsigned int projectorMap

GL 2D texture id; 0 disables. Not owned by the light.

float projectorStrength

Blend toward the projector color, [0, 1]; 0 disables.

glm::vec4 projectorUvScaleOffset

Projector UV transform: uv * xy + zw.

Camera-distance fade

When enabled, non-directional lights fade out smoothly over [distanceFadeBegin, distanceFadeBegin + distanceFadeLength] of camera distance.

inline Light()

Default constructor creates a directional light.

No GL resources are created here; the shadow framebuffer is allocated on first use, so construction does not need a GL context.

  • diffColor – Diffuse color (linear RGB).

Configure as a point light.

inline void setSpotAngles(float innerDeg, float outerDeg)

Set the spotlight cone half-angles in degrees.

Convenience wrapper around the raw cosine fields. The inner cone is the fully-lit region; intensity falls off smoothly between innerDeg and outerDeg. Pass any values; they are clamped so that innerDeg <= outerDeg.

Parameters:

  • innerDeg – Half-angle in degrees where falloff begins.

  • outerDeg – Half-angle in degrees where light reaches zero.

inline void setRange(float rangeMeters)

Set the attenuation of a point, spot or area light from its range in metres.

Sets the inverse-quadratic coefficients 1, 4.5/range and 75/range^2: full intensity at the source, about 1% (1/80.5) at the range, and still decreasing beyond it (it never reaches zero, and the range does not limit which objects the light shades). Use this instead of writing constant/linear/quadratic by hand. radius, the source size, is not changed.

Parameters:

rangeMeters – Distance at which the light contribution falls to about 1%.

bool ensureShadowFramebuffer()

Create or resize the shadow framebuffer and 2D depth texture.

Requires a current OpenGL context. Resources created in a different context are discarded and recreated.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – (via the framebuffer completeness check) if the framebuffer is incomplete; resources are discarded in that case.

Returns:

Always true.

bool shadowPrePass()

Prepare for 2D shadow depth rendering.

Ensures the framebuffer, updates lightSpaceMatrix_, binds the FBO, sets the viewport, clears depth, enables polygon offset and disables face culling (restored by shadowPostPass()). Requires a current GL context.

Returns:

Always true; failures throw as in ensureShadowFramebuffer().

void updateShadowMatrix(int snapResolution)

Recompute lightSpaceMatrix_ (used by standalone shadow maps and atlas tiles).

Directional lights use an orthographic box (see setShadowOrtho()) around the shadow center; spot lights a perspective frustum fitted to the outer cone; area lights a 150 degree frustum; point lights a 90 degree frustum.

Parameters:

snapResolution – Shadow-map resolution in texels used to snap directional shadows to the texel grid (reduces shimmering).

bool pointShadowPrePassFace(int face)

Prepare one face of a point-light cubemap shadow render.

Updates lightSpaceMatrix_ and the face’s entry in pointLightSpaceMatrices_, then binds that cubemap face for depth rendering. Requires a current GL context.

Parameters:

face – Cubemap face index in OpenGL order [0, 5] (clamped).

Returns:

Always true; failures throw std::runtime_error.

void shadowPostPass()

Restore the caller’s face-cull state, disable polygon offset and bind the default framebuffer after shadow rendering.

Set shadow-map resolution.

Releases existing shadow resources when the value changes; they are recreated at the new size on the next pre-pass.

Parameters:

class Material

A general-purpose material class supporting PBR, textured, and simple color models.

Plain data: every field is public and read when the material is drawn. usesPbrShading() decides the shader: a material whose type is SIMPLE_COLOR or TEXTURED and whose other fields keep their defaults is drawn by the cheaper simple mesh shader, while Type::PBR (the default) or any PBR-only feature selects the PBR shader; forceSimpleShading overrides both. Texture fields hold OpenGL texture ids that the material does not own (0 = unused). Colors are linear RGB(A) in [0, 1] unless noted.

bool receivesActiveWeather() const

True when this material actually picks up weather (wetness/snow).

Mirrors the per-material weather gate in the full PBR fragment shader: a non-PBR or non-porous material, or one that opts out of both wetness and snow, receives no weather effect — so it does not require the weather-capable full shader even when weather is globally enabled. Used by the scene-level shader selection so a per-material weather opt-out actually preserves the core/foliage-fast path (it previously did not).

Public Static Functions

static Material pbr(std::string name, const glm::vec4 &baseColor, float metallic = 0.0f, float roughness = 0.5f)

Build a metallic/roughness PBR material with sensible defaults.

Sets type = Type::PBR, the albedo tint, metallic, and roughness factors; leaves all texture slots empty. Provide an IBL environment separately via Visuals::setPbrEnvironment(...) if you want indirect lighting.

Parameters:

  • name – Material name.

  • baseColor – Linear RGBA albedo tint.

  • metallic – Metallic factor in [0, 1].

  • roughness – Roughness factor in [0, 1].

Returns:

The configured material.

static Material glass(std::string name = "Glass", float thickness = 0.0f, const glm::vec3 &tint = glm::vec3(1.0f), float attenuationDistance = 1.0f, float roughness = 0.04f, float indexOfRefraction = 1.5f)

Dielectric glass. Zero thickness represents a thin window; positive thickness is an authored world-space optical path length for a solid. Tint is the transmitted color after attenuationDistance world units. Keep alpha at one: transmission, not coverage, makes glass transparent. Enable RenderQualitySettings::screenSpaceRefraction for scene transmission. Sets transmissionFactor = 1 and metallic = 0; a thin pane (thickness <= 0) is also made double-sided.

Parameters:

  • name – Material name.

  • thickness – Optical path length in world units (clamped to >= 0).

  • tint – Transmitted color, clamped to [0, 1].

  • attenuationDistance – Distance at which tint is reached (min 1e-4).

  • roughness – Surface roughness.

  • indexOfRefraction – IOR, clamped to [1, 3].

Returns:

The configured material.

static Material unlitColor(std::string name, const glm::vec4 &color = glm::vec4(1.0f))

Build an unlit material that ignores scene lighting.

Useful for HUD elements, debug visuals, holograms, light-emitting decals. Named unlitColor rather than unlit to avoid colliding with the bool unlit data member. Sets unlit, which selects the PBR shader’s unlit path.

Parameters:

  • name – Material name.

  • color – Linear RGBA color.

Returns:

The configured material.

static Material simpleColor(std::string name, const glm::vec4 &color)

Build a simple-color (non-PBR) material that responds to lighting.

Routes through the simple mesh shader (sets forceSimpleShading). Cheaper than pbr() and appropriate for primitives that do not need metallic/roughness or IBL.

Parameters:

  • color – Linear RGBA color.

Returns:

The configured material.

static Material foliage(std::string name, FoliageType foliageKind, const glm::vec4 &baseColor)

Build a foliage material with the given type and base color.

Sets foliageType, a PBR type with roughness 0.85 and metallic 0, and doubleSided (no culling, two-sided lighting). Other foliage fields keep their defaults; in particular foliageWindStrength stays 0, so there is no wind deformation until it is set.

Parameters:

  • name – Material name.

  • foliageKind – Foliage category.

  • baseColor – Linear RGBA albedo tint.

Returns:

The configured material.

static Material defaultGround(std::string name = "GroundMaterial")

Build a neutral PBR ground material (mid-grey, rough, non-metallic).

Convenient default for the world’s ground plane / heightmap when no authored material is supplied. Base color 0.55 grey, roughness 0.9, metallic 0.

Parameters:

name – Material name.

Returns:

The configured material.

struct RenderQualitySettings

Explicit runtime quality settings for viewer rendering.

The struct stores its fields as a flat layout for historical reasons; the flat fields are the source of truth. For authoring, new code may use the grouped sub-config accessors — shadows(), bloom(), depthOfField(), fog(), toneMapping(), temporalAa() — and the matching set*() writers, which copy to and from the flat fields.

Use RenderQualitySettings::preset(RenderQualityPreset) to start from a known-good configuration, then apply with RayraiWindow::setRenderQualitySettings(). That call clamps many fields to the ranges noted on them and throws std::invalid_argument for invalid temporal-AA parameters; the remaining noted ranges are applied when the value is uploaded to the shaders.

Background and main light

The main light is directional. Struct defaults are what Fast and Custom start from; in the simple-shading path there is no IBL, so a moderate ambient keeps smooth/metallic surfaces from going black.

Clear color, RGBA in 0..255 (shown where no sky/environment is drawn).

Main light ambient color (linear RGB); also the sky fill on the simple-shading path.

Main light diffuse color/intensity (linear RGB); also tints the procedural sky sun.

Main light specular color (linear RGB).

Direction the main light travels (from the light toward the scene); normalized on apply, ignored if zero.

Main directional shadow

The shadow box is an orthographic volume of half-size shadowOrthoHalfSize centered shadowCenterOffset metres in front of the camera. Ranges in brackets are applied by RayraiWindow::setRenderQualitySettings().

Shading, tone mapping and color

Shading path selection, tone curve, exposure and post-process color controls.

Display gamma: output = pow(color, 1 / gamma); at least 0.01.

Render every mesh with the simple (non-PBR) shader.

Tone curve used when pbrToneMapping is on.

Exposure multiplier applied before the tone curve.

Adapt exposure from the average brightness of the previous frame.

Target average luminance of the displayed frame (approximately linear).

Fraction of the remaining exposure error corrected per frame, [0, 1].

Lower bound of the auto-exposure multiplier.

float autoExposureMaxFactor

Upper bound of the auto-exposure multiplier.

Post-process saturation, 1 = unchanged, 0 = grayscale (>= 0).

Color-grade look applied at the end of the post chain.

Blend between ungraded and graded color, [0, 1].

Environment lighting and sky

Image-based lighting and the procedural sky. Environment mips are chosen as clamp(maxLod * r * (2 - r) + bias, 0, maxLod) for roughness r.

Highest environment mip used for rough reflections; 0 always samples mip 0.

Bias added to the roughness-based environment mip, [-1, 2].

Rotation of environment maps and the sky about world +Z, radians.

float pbrEnvironmentIntensity

Image-based lighting intensity multiplier (high-fidelity PBR).

glm::vec3 pbrEnvironmentLightingTint

Linear RGB illumination for the procedural fallback, independent of the visible sky/fog palette. HDR environment maps retain their captured color.

glm::vec3 pbrEnvironmentSkyTint

Tint of the upper sky in the background and procedural environment.

glm::vec3 pbrEnvironmentHorizonTint

Tint of the horizon band.

glm::vec3 pbrEnvironmentGroundTint

Tint of the lower hemisphere (ground).

float pbrEnvironmentHorizonStrength

Width/strength of the horizon band, [0, 1].

glm::vec3 environmentBackgroundTint

Tint applied to the drawn sky/environment background (>= 0).

Brightness multiplier of the drawn sky/environment background (>= 0).

Brightness of the procedural sun disk (>= 0).

Angular radius of the procedural sun disk, radians.

Shadow budget, cascades and additional shadows

Additional lights get shadow maps in order of their score, up to shadowedLightBudget - 1. Ranges in brackets are applied by RayraiWindow::setRenderQualitySettings().

bool shadowsEnabled

Master switch for shadow rendering.

int shadowedLightBudget

Shadowed lights including the main light; budget - 1 additional lights get shadow maps (max 8).

PointShadowPolicy pointShadowPolicy

Whether point lights can receive shadow maps.

int maxPointShadowLights

Maximum point lights with shadow cubemaps, [0, 8].

float additionalShadowResolutionScale

Additional spot/directional/area shadow-map size relative to shadowResolution.

float pointShadowResolutionScale

Point-light cube face size relative to shadowResolution.

int minAdditionalShadowResolution

Lower bound for additional shadow-map sizes, texels.

float shadowSlopeBiasScale

Slope-scaled depth bias, [0, 4].

float shadowNormalOffset

Receiver normal offset for shadow lookups, metres, [0, 0.02].

int directionalShadowCascadeCount

Directional shadow cascades, [1, 4]; 1 = single shadow map.

float directionalShadowCascadeLambda

Split blend, [0, 1]: 0 = uniform, 1 = logarithmic.

float directionalShadowCascadeMaxDistance

Shadowed view distance, metres; 0 uses shadowFar.

std::array<float, 4> directionalShadowCascadeSplitOverrides

Explicit split distances (metres) between cascades; used only if strictly increasing within range.

float additionalShadowBiasScale

Additional (non-point) shadow bias = shadowBias * scale.

float additionalShadowStrengthScale

Directional extras: shadowStrength * scale; spot/area/point: used directly as strength, [0, 1].

float additionalShadowPcfRadiusScale

Additional shadow PCF radius = shadowPcfRadius * scale.

float additionalShadowNormalOffsetScale

Additional shadow normal offset relative to shadowNormalOffset, [0, 4].

Pack additional 2D shadow maps into one atlas.

Shadow atlas edge length, texels, [512, 16384].

int additionalShadowAtlasPadding

Gap between atlas tiles, texels, [0, 16].

float pointShadowBiasScale

Point-light shadow bias = shadowBias * scale.

float pointShadowFar

Point-light shadow far plane, metres.

bool updateShadowsEveryFrame

Re-render shadow maps every frame; otherwise only when the scene, light or camera moves enough.

Additional-light selection

int maxAdditionalLightsPerFrame

Additional lights shaded per frame, [0, 16], chosen by influence near the view.

float minAdditionalLightInfluence

Additional lights with an influence score at or below this are skipped.

float additionalLightContributionThreshold

Opt-in total scene-linear incident-radiance cutoff budget for local additional lights, before the material BRDF and exposure. Zero preserves unlimited lighting exactly. Not a bound on final HDR/specular pixel error. The budget is divided among uploaded lights; fade starts below that share.

Public Static Functions

static RenderQualitySettings preset(RenderQualityPreset p)

Build a RenderQualitySettings for the given preset.

Companion to the existing RenderQualityPreset enum so the type that names the presets can also produce them. Delegates to RayraiWindow::defaultRenderQualitySettings() (defined in RenderQualityDefaults.cpp). The result is not clamped until it is passed to RayraiWindow::setRenderQualitySettings().

Parameters:

p – Preset to build.

Returns:

Struct defaults with the preset’s overrides applied.

enum class raisin::RenderQualityPreset

Viewer-quality policy presets (RenderQualitySettings::preset()).

These presets affect interactive viewer rendering only. They do not change sensor world-object filtering or make sensor outputs include viewer-only visuals.

Values:

enumerator Fast

Simple (non-PBR) shading, texture clouds, no reflective ground.

enumerator Balanced

PBR + IBL with ACES tone mapping, texture clouds, reflective ground; no MSAA/SSAO/DoF/TAA.

enumerator High

Adds 2x MSAA, volumetric clouds, SSAO, DoF, FXAA, probe filtering, two shadowed lights.

enumerator Ultra

High plus 4x MSAA, AgX tone curve, TAA, larger shadow maps and probe filters.

enumerator Custom

Struct defaults plus texture clouds; also reported after any manual settings change.

enum class raisin::ViewerColorMode

Tone curve applied when RenderQualitySettings::pbrToneMapping is enabled.

With tone mapping disabled the mode has no effect.

Values:

enumerator FastLinear

Currently uses the same fitted ACES curve as AcesApprox.

enumerator AcesApprox

Fitted ACES filmic curve.

enumerator UnrealPreviewApprox

ACES with slight shadow lift and highlight desaturation.

enumerator FilmicApprox

Hejl/Burgess-Dawson style filmic curve.

enumerator AgXApprox

AgX-style log curve; hue-preserving and neutral.

enum class raisin::ColorGradePreset

ASC-CDL color grade presets applied at the end of the post-process chain.

No grading.

Warm highlights, slight teal shadows.

enumerator Cool

Cyan/blue cast.

enumerator Cinematic

Teal shadows, orange highlights.

enumerator Bleach

Low saturation, slight green push (bleach bypass).

Weather, scene effects, and reflections

struct WeatherSettings

Weather state applied on top of the renderer (RayraiWindow::setWeatherSettings()).

While enabled is true the window re-derives its effective RenderQualitySettings from the last settings passed to setRenderQualitySettings() every time weather changes: the main light (sun/moon direction and color), ambient, procedural sky and clouds, environment tints/intensity, exposure, cloud shadows and the wet/snow material fields are overwritten, while fog density, height fog and volumetric fog/lighting are combined with the user values (the larger density wins). Disabling weather restores the user settings.

Values are clamped by setWeatherSettings() (ranges noted per field). Several effects are driven by timeOfDayHours, so advance it to animate lightning, cloud drift, rain ripples and volumetric fog.

struct ProjectedDecal

Screen-space box decal blended over the opaque scene in the post-process pass.

The decal box is centered at center, rotated by orientation and sized by halfExtents (metres). Surfaces inside the box receive the decal. The decal projects along the box’s local +Z axis: the decal UV comes from local X/Y, and surfaces facing away from local +Z are faded out by normalFade. Values are sanitized by RayraiWindow::addProjectedDecal() (ranges noted per field).

Public Members

glm::vec3 center

World-space box center, metres.

glm::vec3 halfExtents

Box half-size per local axis, metres (abs, >= 0.001).

glm::mat3 orientation

Box rotation (columns = local axes); re-orthonormalized on add.

glm::vec4 color

Linear RGB tint (clamped to [0, 4]) and opacity in alpha ([0, 1]).

float edgeFade

Fraction of the box (in normalized local units) faded at its faces, [0.001, 0.95].

float normalFade

Facing fade: opacity ramps in as local-space normal Z goes 0..normalFade, [0.001, 1].

float upperFade

Extra fade toward the box’s local +Y face, as a fraction of the half-extent; 0 disables.

float lowerFade

Extra fade toward the box’s local -Y face, as a fraction of the half-extent; 0 disables.

unsigned int albedoMap

Optional GL 2D texture multiplied with color; 0 = none.

unsigned int emissionMap

Optional GL 2D emission texture added to the decal color; 0 = none.

Optional GL 2D tangent-space normal map (approximate relief shading); 0 = none.

Optional GL 2D occlusion/roughness/metallic texture (R/G/B); 0 = none.

UV transform (scale.xy, offset.zw) applied to all decal maps.

Blend from color toward albedoMap * color, [0, 1].

Multiplier for emissionMap, >= 0.

normalMap intensity, [0, 2].

ormMap influence, [0, 1].

Fade the decal out with camera distance to center.

Distance from the camera where the fade starts, metres.

Length of the smooth fade band, metres.

struct ReflectionProbe

Static local reflection probe registered with RayraiWindow::addReflectionProbe().

Usually produced by RayraiWindow::captureFilteredReflectionProbe(). A probe takes part in selection only when at least one of its cubemaps is non-zero. Its weight at a point is strength * (1 - d / radius) (zero beyond radius), or strength / (1 + d) when radius is 0, where d is the distance to position, or to the box when box projection is enabled and the box is non-degenerate (so d is 0 inside the box).

Public Members

glm::vec3 position

Capture position, metres.

float radius

Influence radius, metres; 0 = unbounded inverse-distance falloff.

unsigned int environmentMap

Radiance cubemap (RGBA8 and mipmapped when captured by rayrai).

unsigned int irradianceMap

Filtered diffuse irradiance cubemap; 0 if not filtered.

unsigned int prefilteredEnvironmentMap

GGX-prefiltered specular cubemap; 0 if not filtered.

unsigned int brdfLut

Split-sum BRDF LUT texture; 0 if not generated.

float strength

Weight/intensity multiplier, >= 0.

bool boxProjection

Use box-projected (parallax-corrected) lookups and box-distance weighting.

glm::vec3 boxMin

Projection box minimum corner, world space, metres.

glm::vec3 boxMax

Projection box maximum corner, world space, metres.

Probe capture is never automatic. Applications call captureReflectionProbeCubemap() when they want a bounded real-time local reflection approximation. Custom visuals, instanced visuals, and point clouds are captured only when their draw toggles are enabled and they are marked detectable.

struct ReflectionProbeFilterSettings

Explicit CPU filtering settings for captured local reflection probes.

Filtering is a load-time/manual operation run by captureFilteredReflectionProbe(). When no filter settings are passed, they are derived from the RenderQualitySettings::reflectionProbe* fields, which only the High and Ultra presets enable; otherwise every size is 0 and only the raw cubemap is captured. Render quality, weather, capture, reflection-probe, and diagnostics helpers are exposed through raisin::RayraiWindow and the public headers included by rayrai/RayraiWindow.hpp. The sections above document the intended entry points and the fast-path boundaries for those APIs.

RaiSim integration

class RaisimObject

Render wrapper for a raisim::Object.

RaisimObject caches meshes and per-shape scales for a raisim object and exposes a draw method that respects appearance and collision-visual toggles.

Material queries

Internal: renderer pass-selection queries over all cached meshes.

Highest Material::renderPriority across cached meshes (0 if none).

Public Functions

explicit RaisimObject(raisim::Object *object, RayraiWindow *parent, std::shared_ptr<RayraiGlobalAsset> asset)

Construct a render wrapper for a raisim object.

Builds or fetches the geometry for every visual (articulated systems get both visual and collision meshes). Primitive and file meshes come from asset and are shared with other objects; meshes of objects whose appearance is hidden at creation may be loaded lazily when shown. Requires a current GL context.

Parameters:

  • object – Raisim object to wrap (not owned; must be non-null).

  • parent – Owning RayraiWindow (for shared assets/settings).

  • asset – Asset cache to load primitive/mesh geometry.

void draw(Shader &shader, bool showCollisionBodies, OpenGLMesh::RenderMode mode = OpenGLMesh::RenderMode::All, uint64_t renderSerial = 0)

Draw the object using the provided shader.

Sets the shadingType, model and objectColor uniforms per mesh; the shader must already be in use. No-op when hidden or invalid.

Parameters:

  • shader – Shader used for rendering.

  • showCollisionBodies – True to render collision geometry when available (articulated systems only).

  • mode – Which material passes of each mesh to draw.

  • renderSerial – Frame serial used to upload deformable geometry at most once per frame; 0 always re-syncs.

bool isSelectable() const

Check if this object can be selected in the picker.

Returns:

True if valid, not hidden, and not a heightmap or ground plane.

inline bool isValid() const

True when this wrapper still references a live raisim::Object.

RaisimObject does not own the underlying raisim object; if the world it came from is destroyed or the object removed, the cached pointer becomes dangling. Public mutators (updateAppearance, updateHeightMapVisual, configureGroundMaterial) early-return when isValid() is false so callers don’t have to track lifetime themselves. Clear the underlying pointer via invalidate() when the source object is removed.

Returns:

True while the wrapped object pointer is set.

inline void invalidate()

Mark this wrapper as no longer referencing a live raisim::Object.

Subsequent calls to mutators become no-ops. The owning RayraiWindow uses this when the world is reset or an object is removed.

bool updateAppearance()

Refresh appearance (color and hidden state) from the underlying raisim object.

Single-body objects only; articulated systems are ignored.

Returns:

True when the color or hidden state changed.

bool updateHeightMapVisual()

Refresh a heightmap object’s existing mesh vertices without rebuilding its mesh.

Uploads only the heightmap’s visual dirty rows when available, otherwise all vertices. Triangles touching NaN or infinite heights are omitted; their index buffer is refreshed when holes appear or disappear. Requires a current GL context.

Returns:

False if this is not a heightmap or its samples are unavailable.

void configureGroundMaterial(bool reflective, float roughness, float metallic, bool proceduralChecker = false)

Configure ground and heightmap terrain materials. No-op for other objects.

For a ground plane, resets its material and makes it PBR with planar reflection when reflective, or simple/textured otherwise. For a heightmap, only the window’s terrain overrides are reapplied and the other arguments are ignored.

Parameters:

  • reflective – Use a reflective PBR ground.

  • roughness – PBR roughness, clamped to [0.04, 1] (reflective only).

  • metallic – PBR metallic factor, clamped to [0, 1] (reflective only).

  • proceduralChecker – Draw a procedural checker instead of the ground texture.
